sources: Walkthrough: 'Find a way through the Sewers so you can search for the Sun Orb'; Maramoa: 'there exists a pair of ancient treasures, the Sun Orb and the Moon Orb. They are our hope… our desperation.'

nodes.name: Tolman's Failed Resurrection
nodes.summary: Clarissa's ritual with the Ankh fails; the exile must kill the resurrected Tolman.

nodes.name: Entering the Beast's Belly
nodes.summary: Sin burns a new entrance into the Beast's corpse using Basilisk acid and mining powder.

nodes.name: The Exile Kills the Depraved Trinity
nodes.summary: The three harvested souls merge into the Depraved Trinity in the Rotting Core and are destroyed; Lilly then offers passage to Oriath.

nodes.name: Kira's Rite and Garukhan's Death
nodes.summary: The exile kills Kira and Garukhan but fails to save Oyun; the Feather goes to Tasuni or Irasha.

nodes.name: The Exile Kills Shakari
nodes.summary: Using Garukhan's bottled storm the exile clears the sandstorm and kills Shakari.

nodes.name: Recurring Nightmare
nodes.summary: Required Act 9 quest. Sin asks the Exile to gather Basilisk Acid and Trarthan Powder (Refinery, Boiling Lake) so he can burn a new entrance into the Beast. The Exile meets Sin at the Quarry, enters the Belly of the Beast, and kills the Depraved Trinity; Lilly Roth then offers to ferry the Exile to Oriath for Act 10.
sources: walkthrough: 'Talk to Sin in Highgate about the Beast and what to do'; 'Meet Sin at the Quarry, where he will burn open a new entrance into the Belly of the Beast'; completion: 'You have killed the Depraved Trinity. Now talk to Lilly to gain access to Act 10'; Lilly Roth: 'Say the words and we'll set the sails.'

nodes.name: The Ruler of Highgate
nodes.summary: Optional Act 9 quest. Kira has kidnapped Oyun to sacrifice her to Garukhan. The Exile kills Kira and Garukhan but cannot save Oyun; the Sekhema Feather is then given to Tasuni or Irasha (the Exile's choice), who rules Highgate. The reward is a Book of Skill.
sources: lead: 'an optional quest in act 9'; walkthrough: 'Kira has kidnapped Oyun and plans to sacrifice her to Garukhan'; completion lines: 'You have given the Sekhema Feather to Tasuni and he now rules Highgate' / 'to Irasha and she now rules Highgate'; 'failed to save Oyun'

nodes.name: A Choice of Futures
nodes.summary: Tutorial quest for the Ultimatum mechanic (Ultimatum league). In a map, the Exile approaches an entity of Chaos, chooses one of the Trialmaster's challenges, completes the round without leaving the ritual circle, and decides whether to raise the difficulty or leave with the current reward.
sources: infobox: start 'Any map with Trialmaster', objective 'Start Ultimatum encounter'; walkthrough: 'Your path has led you to an entity of Chaos. Approach him.'; 'Complete the Trialmaster's (round number) challenge without leaving the ritual circle'

nodes.name: Karui Shores and the Atlas of Worlds
nodes.summary: The exile reaches Karui Shores and starts mapping.

nodes.name: The Eldritch Decay
nodes.summary: Final Atlas quest given by Zana in the epilogue. The Exile spreads Elder influence to the four Tier 16 Shaper Guardian maps so the Elder spawns in the Shaper's Realm, then defeats the Elder Guardians and the Uber Elder. Removed from the game in 3.9.0 when the Atlas mechanic was reworked (introduced 3.2.0).
sources: infobox: start 'Talk to Zana', completion 'Talk to Zana', act 'Epilogue'; section 'Walkthrough': 'Defeat the Elder (Uber Elder)'; Version history 3.9.0 'Removed from the game'

nodes.name: Oriath after Kitava (older Epilogue, v3.9-3.16)
nodes.summary: Historical content (removed in 3.17): in the earlier Epilogue the exile talks to Officer Kirac in rebuilding Oriath, who asks them to investigate his brother Baran's disappearance and Zana at the Templar Laboratory, leading to the Vault of Venarius and a rebuilt Map Device. Kitava's skull is displayed in Oriath (Epilogue).
sources: Gallery: Kitava's skull on display in Oriath (Epilogue)

nodes.name: The Sacred Grove (quest)
nodes.summary: Introductory quest for the Harvest mechanic. After the Exile finds the Sacred Grove, Oshabi teaches the Exile to harvest the Grove's seeds (Wild, Vivid and Primal Lifeforce pools), kill the monsters that emerge, and talk to her about the harvest. Reworked in 3.13.0.
sources: infobox: start 'The Sacred Grove', objective 'Talk to Oshabi about how to harvest the Grove's seeds', act 'Epilogue'; quest logs: 'Activate the Lifeforce Collector ... Kill the monsters that have emerged from the Seeds'; Version history 3.13.0 'Reworked'
section 'Quests': 'Oshabi offers players the following quest: The Sacred Grove'

nodes.name: Sailing Away from Oriath
nodes.summary: After Kitava's death Lilly Roth, in a class-specific line, offers to sail the exile away from Oriath and the quest 'Toward the Future' leads to the Epilogue.

nodes.name: The Memory Eater
nodes.summary: Epilogue quest given by Zana. The Exile must collect 15 Memory Fragments by killing the bosses of Elder-influenced Atlas maps; each fragment can be exchanged for a Shaper's Orb, and each turn-in earns Zana reputation, and fragments II to X also earn a map of the same tier as the fragment. Removed in 3.9.0.
sources: lead paragraph: 'a quest given by Zana in the story's epilogue ... collect 15 Memory Fragments by killing the bosses of 15 maps'; infobox start 'Speak to Zana'; Version history 3.9.0 'Removed from the game'

nodes.name: The Redeemer (quest)
nodes.summary: Epilogue Atlas quest in which Zana's former colleague Veritania has gone insane and lurks in corner-region maps of the Atlas. The Exile finds her three times, then uses Kirac's information and Zana's portals to enter her Citadel and defeat Veritania the Redeemer. Reworked for 3.16 when the Atlas was reduced to four regions; removed in 3.17.
sources: infobox: start 'Complete The Elderslayers', boss 'Veritania'; walkthrough: 'The third time you do, Veritania will appear and taunt the player'; 'talk to Kirac ... talk to Zana to open six portals into Veritania's Citadel'; Version history: reworked as regions reduced to 4; removed in 3.17

nodes.name: The Lost Expedition (quest)
nodes.summary: Act 6 quest started by Dannig: the exile finds ancient Kalguuran texts and learns the expedition's story. The Triskelion Flame is located and destroyed in defeating Olroth. Introduced in Expedition league (3.15.0).

nodes.name: Pound of Flesh
nodes.summary: Epilogue Metamorph-league quest. Tane Octavius asks the Exile to slay monsters and collect five different Metamorph organ samples; the samples summon a Metamorph which the Exile defeats. Afterwards Tane can be invited to the hideout and the Tane's Laboratory is accessible.
sources: infobox: act 'Epilogue', start 'Map', objective 'Tane wants you to slay creatures and collect samples ... five different samples'; walkthrough: 'Your samples have summoned a Metamorph! Defeat it.'; 'the player character can access the Tane's Laboratory after the quest'

nodes.name: Shattered Past
nodes.summary: Act 1 quest exclusive to the Synthesis league (historical; removed in 3.7.0). Cavas, an amnesiac, asks the Exile to explore and stabilise a corrupted memory and find more memories; once he remembers enough, the Exile is given access to the Memory Nexus.
sources: lead: 'was a quest in Act 1 exclusive to the Synthesis league'; Cavas: 'Oh. Oh dear. Oh DEAR! I've remembered something! Exile, it is time we go to the Nexus.'; 'Quest Complete - You have gained access to the Memory Nexus'

nodes.name: Strange Growths
nodes.summary: Blight tutorial quest (Act 3 or any Blight encounter). Sister Cassia asks the Exile to activate her Ichor Pump; the Exile builds towers near the Mycelium and defends the pump from Fungal Defenders. Completing it unlocks Anointing.
sources: infobox: act 3, start 'Any Map (except Blighted Map) with the presence of Cassia'; walkthrough: 'Build a Tower near the Mycelium to help protect Cassia's pump'; 'Quest Complete - You have helped Cassia defend her Ichor Pump'; quest unlocks 'anointing'

nodes.name: The Undertaker's Apprentice
nodes.summary: Tutorial quest for the Necropolis league mechanic. The Exile kills monsters until a usable corpse drops, buries it in The Necropolis, performs the exorcism by digging the grave, and returns to Undertaker Arimor to end the quest.
sources: infobox: start 'Approach Undertaker Arimor', objective 'Collect corpse / Perform the Exorcism in The Necropolis', completion 'Talk to Undertaker Arimor', act 1; walkthrough: 'Perform the Exorcism by digging the grave in the Necropolis'

nodes.name: Assault on Oriath (planned Act 5)
nodes.summary: Announced Act 5: arrive in Oriath hunting the Beast; datamined quests The Siege of Oriath, Infiltrating Oriath, etc.

nodes.name: Gods awaken after the Beast's death
nodes.summary: About 20 years before PoE2 an exile killed the Beast, waking the slumbering gods, who per the Twilight Order now make civilisation impossible.

nodes.name: Trial of the Ancestors (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional PoE2 Act 4 quest unlocked by freeing Matiki; the Exile meets Hinekora in the Trial of the Ancestors and receives the Tattoo of Hinekora.

alt_summaries.summary: Matiki's rescue leads to Tests of Mettle, Yama's trial and Hinekora, who offers 'Her power... if you will accept it.'

nodes.name: Precursor Cataclysm
nodes.summary: After mastering corruption the Precursors delved into world secrets, triggering great fires, eruptions and impacts from the sky; the civilisation was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm. Cause unclear.

nodes.name: Priesthood conspiracy (stabbing of Olroth)
nodes.summary: High Priest Uhtred, suspecting Olroth of fighting for the horrors in his sleep, had a dozen priests stab him (71 wounds); Vorana killed all twelve; Olroth was encased in glass and Uhtred fled to an ancient site of power.

nodes.name: Purity Rebellion
nodes.summary: A rebellion led by High Templar Voll and the poet Victario, with King Kaom, Sekhema Deshret and Thane Rigwald. It culminates in the siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC) and Voll's coronation.
sources: sections 'The Purity Rebellion', 'Siege of Sarn', 'Assassination of Chitus'
issues #1-4 (Death to Sin / The Black Heart)

alt_summaries.summary: Voll's crusade against Gemlings.

nodes.name: Rapture Device activation
nodes.summary: 1336 IC; Dialla refuses; Malachai enters Beast.

nodes.name: The Red Communion
nodes.summary: Project that allowed Atziri to commune directly with the Beast. Doryani, privately opposed, was forced to devise it; he learned all he could and prepared contingencies. It triggered the Vaal Cataclysm.
sources: Spymaster note: 'consequences of the Red Communion'

nodes.name: Return of the Sun
nodes.summary: The Winter of the World ends: Maraketh tradition credits twin sekhema Solerai and Lundara expelling the Lightless; official Abyss text credits Solaris. Sources differ (possibly the same figures).
sources: The Lightless final paragraph; The Maraketh

nodes.name: The Searing Exarch (quest)
nodes.summary: Epilogue quest added in 3.17.0 and run in parallel with The Maven and The Eater of Worlds quests. The Envoy gives the Luminous Astrolabe, which lets the Exile add Searing Exarch influence to Tier 9 to 16 maps. The Tier 11 map boss drops a Polaric Invitation to the Black Star's arena (area level 79); the Tier 16 map boss drops an Incandescent Invitation to the Searing Exarch's arena (The Absence of Patience and Wisdom). The Black Star is defeated first, then the Searing Exarch. The quest pays out Atlas passive points (2 skill points, 4 respec points on completion) and an Omniscient Voidstone via Kirac; the Exarch drops an Eldritch Voidstone if The Eater of Worlds was defeated first.

chronology.relative: PoE1 endgame (3.17.0 Siege of the Atlas)

sources: infobox (boss The Searing Exarch) and Walkthrough: quest intro 'This quest runs in parallel to The Maven (quest) and The Eater of Worlds (quest)'; 'Use the Luminous Astrolabe', 'Polaric Invitation', 'Incandescent Invitation' steps; Quest Complete log 'You have gained 2 Atlas Passive Skill Points and 4 Atlas Passive Respec Points'; version history 3.17.0

nodes.name: Siege of Sarn
nodes.summary: On the last day of Divini 1334 IC, High Templar Voll laid siege to Sarn with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh rebel support. Cadiro Perandus negotiated Sarn's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC, and Voll was crowned a week later.
sources: section 'Siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC)' and the paragraph after 'Assassination of Chitus' (surrender and coronation)

alt_summaries.summary: Divini 1334 IC; Voll besieges Sarn.

nodes.name: Sin Consults Kalandra
nodes.summary: Sin seeks Kalandra at her lake and receives cryptic instructions leading him to a Precursor ruin holding the Seed of Corruption, used to create the Beast. Etching V's 'little thief' is read as Sin; PoE1 link is inference, PoE2 wiki states it directly.

nodes.name: Slumber of the Gods
nodes.summary: Sin plants the Dark Ember in Highgate, creating the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy. The Beast initiates the Slumber of the Gods, which puts all gods to sleep.

nodes.name: Slumbering of the Gods
nodes.summary: Sin's Beast lulled the gods into dreamless slumber, ending an era of divine strife; Hinekora foresaw it and prepared the Halls of the Dead before sleeping.

chronology.relative: unknown, millennia before PoE1 (before the Vaal Empire per PoE2 wiki)

sources: Sin 'The Rise of the Gods': "We gods, we were driven into slumbering darkness, to dream away eternity whilst the gentle Beast watched over us."
Hinekora dream: 'She foresaw the Slumbering of the Gods' / hinekora wiki Lore

nodes.name: Memory of the Templar Laboratory
nodes.summary: Tier-5+ Synthesis memory in which Cavas sees High Templar Venarius and the scientist Valdo Caeserius building something together; Venarius lashes out, triggering the realisation of Cavas's identity.

chronology.relative: Past of the Templar Laboratory, shortly before Valdo's imprisonment

nodes.name: Templars shift to Oriath
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Templar Theocracy of Oriath
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm, the Templars shift their base to Oriath and develop a theocracy. The Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius shortly before PoE1.

nodes.name: The Maven's Game (quest)
nodes.summary: Epilogue quest that starts when the Exile enters Absence of Mercy and Empathy with a Maven's Writ; it culminates in the Maven pinnacle boss fight. Defeating the Maven unlocks the Ceremonial Voidstone (reported to Commander Kirac); the quest's final steps have the Exile use an Atlas Book of Skill for 1 Atlas passive skill point and 2 Atlas passive respec points.
sources: infobox (required=no, start 'Obtain a The Maven's Writ', completion 'Defeat The Maven') and Walkthrough: quest-log lines 'Challenge the Maven', 'Talk to Commander Kirac', 'Use the Atlas Book of Skill'; version history 3.13.0 'Introduced to the game'
Walkthrough, final paragraph: after the final invitation the player forms 'The Maven's Writ which is used to challenge The Maven'

nodes.name: The Rogue Harbour (quest)
nodes.summary: Act 6 introductory quest for the Heist mechanic: after Kurai and a Rogue's Marker, the Exile opens a portal to The Rogue Harbour, takes Contract: Trial Run from Kurai and finishes it with Karst.
sources: Quest infobox: act 6, required no, start 'Lioneye's Watch (Act 6)', completion 'Talk to Kurai after finishing the contract'; Version history 3.12.0 'Introduced to the game'

nodes.name: Threads of the Originator
nodes.summary: Epilogue quest starting the Secrets of the Atlas storyline; the Exile follows Memory Threads with Eagon to find the Originator.

alt_summaries.summary: Eagon and the Exile chase Zana's memory threads, defeat the Incarnations of Neglect, Fear and Dread; the Atlas is shattered.

nodes.name: Titans and Humans Fight the Rising Darkness
nodes.summary: A 'rising darkness' (likely the Lightless after the Winter of the World) attacks Titans and humans; surviving Titans forge weapons and unearth the first virtue gem, but are almost wiped out.

nodes.name: Toward the Future
nodes.summary: Act 10 quest closing the campaign: after defeating Kitava, Lilly Roth in Oriath Docks offers to sail the Exile away; completing it is 'Set Sail from Oriath'.
sources: Quest infobox: act 10, start 'Talk to Lilly Roth in Oriath Docks', completion 'Set Sail from Oriath'; Walkthrough: 'Talk to Lilly Roth after defeating Kitava'

nodes.name: Merchant Wars and War of the Great Families
nodes.summary: Feud between House Keita and House Bardiya that escalated into civil war and ended in a ceasefire and the Merchant Council.

nodes.name: Trarthan Rebellion against Phrecius (870 IC)
nodes.summary: Warlords of Trarthus were executed after Phrecian legions occupied it; four first-generation Trarthans led a war; Karui blockades and Ezomyte sabotage doomed reinforcements; Tyndarus capitulated after two years.

nodes.name: Trarthan War of Independence
nodes.summary: 870-872 IC rebellion against Tyndarus.

nodes.name: Trial of the Ancestors
nodes.summary: Tournament in the Halls of the Dead where the Exile's team of Karui warriors fights teams led by the ten Karui chieftains, destroying totems; winning a full tournament earns rewards from Hinekora (omens, Hinekora's Lock, unique items).
sources: 'rules over the Halls of the Dead and oversees the Trial of the Ancestors'

nodes.name: Trials of Chaos
nodes.summary: Escalating wave trials in which a Trialmaster-set modifier is added each round; the player banks or risks rewards. PoE1 Ultimatum league (3.14), core in 3.23; PoE2 Ascension Trial of Chaos (Act 3 Temple of Chaos, up to 10 trials).

nodes.name: Destruction of the Triskelion Flame
nodes.summary: In defeating Olroth the exile cannot save the Flame, which was keeping him alive; Dannig asks the exile to keep this from the settlers.

nodes.name: Loss of the Triskelion Flame
nodes.summary: The starlight barrier vanished as Vorana tried to adjust it; the Flame's altar was empty and all harbour ships but one had been burned. Vorana branded Uhtred a traitor, and Olroth's glass case was found empty. Uhtred had fled to an ancient shrine.

nodes.name: Turning the Tide
nodes.summary: Endgame Curse of the Allflame quest required to unlock Velka, the Tide Witch: Vesper imbues the Exile with the Allflame to pass Velka's barrier, then the Exile defeats Velka and retrieves her Allflame.
sources: Quest infobox: start 'Explore a Kishara's Rest chart', objective 'Defeat Velka and retrieve her Allflame', act 'Epilogue'; Walkthrough: 'Allow me to imbue you with the power of the Allflame'

nodes.name: Survive the Utzaal Cataclysm through the gateway
nodes.summary: The Exile and Alva survive the Cataclysm in Utzaal's past and return through the gateway with Doryani, who then laments that his people are long dead.

alt_summaries.summary: Doryani, Alva and the Exile use the gateway as the Cataclysm begins ('It begins...'); they return to the present where Doryani sees Utzaal as a grave.

nodes.name: Vaal first contact with the Azmeri
nodes.summary: Around 1160 BC (Trinian, writing c. 1333 IC, says about 2,500 years earlier) the Vaal first contacted the primitive Azmeri tribes of the Azmerian ranges, introducing agriculture and literacy and helping create the first Azmerian written language, while never divulging the secret of virtue gems.

chronology.relative: c. 1160 BC (~2,500 years before Chitus, per Trinian)

sources: section 'Contacting the Azmeri'; Trinian, The Ancients Book 4

nodes.name: Vaal Cataclysm
nodes.summary: Event c. 400 BIC that ended the Vaal Empire: Doryani's project to grant immortality (manipulating the Beast, corruption, gems, sacrifice and 'communion') went wrong; only 3,126 Vaal survived and took refuge with the Azmeri. PoE2 shows the Red Communion and Atziri being swallowed by the Beast.
sources: section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' (paragraph on Path of Exile 2: Fate of the Vaal)
Abilities: 'cutscene... swallowed by the Beast and starting the Cataclysm'

alt_summaries.summary: Doryani's attempt at immortality under Queen Atziri destroys the Vaal Empire. Only 3,126 Vaal survive, and they are absorbed into the Azmeri. In PoE2's Fate of the Vaal league the Exile travels back in time, with Doryani's help, to the moment before the Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Survivors among the Azmeri
nodes.summary: The 3,126 surviving Vaal found refuge among the Azmeri, could not explain what happened, had no gems and assimilated until none remained; they panicked at an image of a gem shown by the Kalguur.

nodes.name: Vastiri Becomes a Desert
nodes.summary: Over thousands of years the plains' rivers dried and forests became sand, naturally or via Maraketh/Halani-linked causes; the Maraketh became semi-nomadic.

nodes.name: Ban on collecting virtue gems in Kalguur
nodes.summary: After the Azmeri reacted fearfully to virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third officially banned their collection; the gems never returned to Kalguur (Kalguur page, Thaumaturgy section).

chronology.relative: during the reign of Cadigan III (ancient Kalguur)

sources: ===Thaumaturgy===: "after witnessing the Azmeris' fearful reaction towards virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third had officially banned their collection"

nodes.name: Voll crowned Emperor
nodes.summary: Voll of Thebrus crowned Emperor in Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC (Eternal Empire page: a week after Cadiro's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci; Purity Chronicles Book 1 says the 2nd Sacrato of Phreci).

nodes.name: Voll's pact with Deshret
nodes.summary: Voll promises Sekhema Deshret the return of the Vastiri Plains for Maraketh support; she demands Titucius' skin for a saddle.

nodes.name: Voll's pact with Kaom
nodes.summary: Voll and Victario visit Kaom in Ngamakanui; Voll promises Karui sovereignty over Wraeclast's south shore and freedom for slaves in exchange for attacking Lioneye's Watch.

nodes.name: Winter of the World
aliases: Winter of the World (Great Fire / Great Wasting)
nodes.summary: Ancient war in which Kulemak and the Lightless blanketed the Vastiri Plains and the surface, ended when the Three Sisters (Solerai/Lundara etc.) destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun.
sources: paragraph 1: 'Winter of the World ... lasted for centuries'
Great Fire: 'revealed that the Great Fire was indeed the same event as the Winter of the World'

alt_summaries.summary: Volcanic eruptions fill the sky with ash. The Lightless attack destroys the primeval civilization, fells the Titans and devastates the Maraketh and Azmeri. The Order of the Djinn later defeats the Lightless.
Initial Abyssal (Lightless) invasion of the surface, ended by the Three Sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun. Minimal node; fuller entry owned by another domain.
Ancient cataclysm of ash, fire and Lightless invasion; PoE2 confirmed the Ezomyte Great Fire is the same event. PoE1 wiki says it was likely caused by the Fourth Edict.

nodes.name: Zana the Originator Fractures the Atlas
nodes.summary: After the Incarnation of Dread, Zana tells Eagon she must destroy the Atlas, 'I am the catalyst', fracturing it into four quadrants and burning its pages; 3.28.0 rendering visible as the destroyed Atlas.
sources: Witness Zana and Eagon; Rewards 3.28 image

nodes.name: Doryani's investigation of Zerphi
nodes.summary: Atziri ordered Doryani to research Zerphi's rejuvenation 'within the realms of possibility... without fear of question or consequence'; Vaal aged 16-26 were sent to him and none survived, the experiments failing.

nodes.name: The Afarud
nodes.summary: Rogue Faridun sect that torments djinn; led by figures such as Ridan, Afarud Commander.

alt_summaries.summary: Outcasts of the Faridun who use forbidden rites and seek destruction of Maraketh and Faridun alike, led by Saresh.

nodes.name: Azmeri
nodes.summary: Ancient tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who worship Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi and others. Eighty thousand of them under Tarcus Veruso descended into the former Vaal lands and founded the Eternal Empire in 1 IC; the Azmeri of the Forest Encampment and the Wildwood descend from those who stayed behind.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the oldest peoples of Wraeclast from the Azmerian Ranges; first lettered by the Vaal, worshipped Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi; their migrants founded the Eternal Empire (only pre-1 IC history counts as 'Azmerian'); Maji remnants in the Wildwood.
Wildwood people.
Tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who took in the Vaal survivors.

nodes.name: Bandit Lords
nodes.summary: Three rival exile bandit leaders extorting the Forest Encampment.

nodes.name: Black Scythe
nodes.summary: Kalguuran mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana, responsible for the expedition's defence and offence. Their artifacts are the currency of the Expedition NPC Tujen.

alt_summaries.summary: Mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana.

nodes.name: Black Scythes
nodes.summary: Kalguuran mercenaries led by Vorana, fighting horrors from walls with crossbows.

nodes.name: Brinerot
nodes.summary: Pirate/whaler warband of the sea whose corsairs ambush chart-seekers; their Shamanessa Velka traffics with the dead.

alt_summaries.summary: Pirates who worship the Brine King and drown mutineers or slaves.

nodes.name: Brotherhood of Silence
nodes.summary: Assassins-for-hire based primarily in Sarn, also called the Silent Brotherhood. The wiki says it acted as a hit squad for many of the Eternal Empire's elite (business with Cadiro and the Perandus family), framed Jorgin for his brother's death so he was exiled from Ogham, and surrounded Drusus in the Bath House until he drowned himself. Listed members: Shadow (former), Coralito and Vorici.
sources: lead paragraph: 'faction of assassins-for-hire based primarily in Sarn'; section 'Lore': 'acted as a hit squad for many of the elite of the Eternal Empire' and the Jorgin and Drusus incidents. Era is not dated on the page (confidence low).

nodes.name: The Caaltu
nodes.summary: A civilisation that existed in Kahuturoa's time (Vastiri still forest, Vaal extant, Oriath recently founded, Ezomyr not yet struck by plague) and was only a memory by Maata's time. Little else is known.

nodes.name: Citizen Vanguard
nodes.summary: Force Kirac leads to defend Wraeclast against coming darkness; over 800 died against Sirus in Siege timeline.

nodes.name: Cultists of Kitava
nodes.summary: Followers of Kitava who plunder refugee ships fleeing Oriath, flood Oriath after its fall (Vilenta lets them into the Overseer's Tower) and hunt for food for their god; the drowned they leave behind wash ashore at the Twilight Strand.
sources: Lilly: cultists have been plundering the refugee ships
Bannon: Kitava's cultists are constantly on the prowl seeking food for their god
Lani: Vilenta led the cultists into the Overseer's Tower

nodes.name: Druids of the Broken Circle
nodes.summary: Kalguuran nature-mystics under Medved, named after Olroth's gem use clouded their scrying.

alt_summaries.summary: Nature-mystics led by Medved; PoE2 names Gronel Starseer, Smalon Thickett, Avon Bruhn.
Kalguuran nature-mystic sect led by Medved, who could see the future by 'peering into the past'. Medved lost that sight the night Olroth set out alone with a gem.

nodes.name: Ebony Legion / Blackguards
nodes.summary: Dominus's Templar soldiers: Ebony Legion and Blackguards who enforce Oriath's rule and hunt in Wraeclast.
sources: Lore: He also controls the Ebony Legion

nodes.name: The Elderslayers
nodes.summary: Group Zana assembled to hunt the Elder: Baran, Veritania, Drox, Al-Hezmin, led by Sirus. They became the Conquerors of the Atlas after going mad.

nodes.name: Eternal Empire
nodes.summary: Oriathan/imperial civilisation, also called the Sarn Empire, founded in 1 IC by Azmeri migrants under Tarcus Veruso on the ruins of the Vaal capital. Ruled by Emperors from Sarn, it held most of central Wraeclast with a Roman-style legion system until the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) destroyed it; Oriath survived as its successor.

chronology.relative: 1 IC to c. 1339 IC; roughly 260 years before PoE1 (1599-1600 IC)

sources: lead paragraph and sections 'History' through 'The Cataclysm'
Act 1: Cemetery of the Eternals / Eternal prison areas

alt_summaries.summary: The Sarn-based Eternal Empire founded by Tarcus Veruso at 1 IC and ruled by Emperors from Sarn. The Cataclysm around 1339 IC ended it.
Old Empire of Wraeclast.

nodes.name: Exiles of Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Convicted Oriathans banished to Wraeclast; survive at Lioneye's Watch and later camps.

nodes.name: Ezomytes
nodes.summary: Clan people of Ezomyr, subjugated and enslaved by the Eternal Empire. Thane Rigwald rallied them in the Bloody Flowers Rebellion of 1333 IC and they joined the siege of Sarn.

alt_summaries.summary: People of Ezomyr and the Isles of Skothe who worship the First Ones; Ezomyr was later largely wiped by plague; speak Ezo.

nodes.name: Faridun
nodes.summary: Maraketh rejects (flawed or mutated newborns left in the dunes) raised by wandering Faridun tribes in the Vastiri, who accept necromancy and long for reunification with the akharas. In PoE2 Act 2 the Countess recruits them with the promise of resurrecting Jamanra.
sources: Overview and Events in Path of Exile 2

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh outcasts left to die in the Vastiri, resentful and necromancy-dabbling; antagonists in PoE2 Act 2.
Desert people of Vastiri set against the Maraketh; featured in PoE2 as well.
Rejected Maraketh outcasts of the Vastiri desert, who ally with the Countess and resurrected Jamanra to feed the Beast.
Faridun sect led by Prince Azmadi, allied with the Serpent Clan avenging Keth's queen.

nodes.name: Gemling Legion
nodes.summary: Elite legions of the Eternal Empire created by Malachai: legionnaires infused with virtue gems, led by Captains, which gave the Empire military dominance. Chitus carried a master gem whose heartbeat bound every gemling to his own, so they fell when he died; survivors were transformed by the Cataclysm into the Undying.

nodes.name: The Godless Three
nodes.summary: Three thaumaturgists trained by Malachai: Shavronne of Umbra, Maligaro the Inquisitor and Doedre Darktongue. Maligaro and Doedre were burned by Voll; Malachai later revived all three to guard his heart, lungs and entrails.

alt_summaries.summary: Malachai's three most loyal servants: Maligaro, Shavronne, Doedre, guarding his organs.

nodes.name: House Azadi
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Contract-assassin monopoly.

nodes.name: House Bardiya
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Financiers; Merchant Council with greatest control today.

nodes.name: House Cyaxan
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Drug trade, criminal syndicate and mass virtue gem implantation.

nodes.name: House Keita
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Slave armies, flesh pits; failed to become a god; founded Korathin 872 IC.

nodes.name: The Immortal Syndicate
nodes.summary: Group of resurrected criminals and the missing forsaken masters under Catarina (the Mastermind), with 17 other members in four divisions (Transportation, Fortification, Research, Intervention); aims to become the ruling power in Wraeclast. Jun believes (not confirmed) the Horns of Kulamac give them their return-from-death ability.

nodes.name: Kalguuran settlers
nodes.summary: Runesmith people of Middengard who built Kingsmarch (Rog, Tujen, Dannig, Gwennen), led by the Cadigan kings; PoE1 Settlers of Kalguur continues into PoE2 Act 4.

alt_summaries.summary: People of Kalguur: rune-smiths who use runes of starlight, have no gods, lack inherent affinity for virtue gems, and live under King Cadigan; settlers in Wraeclast built Kingsmarch.
Seafaring Kalguuran, shown a gem image by Vaal survivors.

nodes.name: Karui
nodes.summary: Seafaring warrior people of the southern archipelago. Under King Kaom they allied with Voll's Purity Rebellion, took Lioneye's Watch and founded the first Karui settlement on the mainland; Kaom later fell at Highgate. The Empire had enslaved Karui under Chitus.

alt_summaries.summary: Nomadic seafaring people of Ngamakanui following the Karui Way; once peaceful farmers and fishermen until Tukohama armed them; ever-changing pantheon; Hinekora made the Halls of the Dead.
Island people of Ngamakanui.

Island people of Ngamakanui (Tukohama, Tasalio, Ngamahu, Tawhoa, Hinekora tribes) who in Act 4 ally with the Exile; ancestors remain in the Halls of the Dead and 'Ngakuramakoi' can be non-Karui by blood.
Island people who obstructed Doryani.

nodes.name: Arohongui tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Arohongui and is led by the chieftain Ikiaho; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Hinekora tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Hinekora and is led by the chieftain Tawhanuku; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Kitava tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Kitava and is led by the chieftain Utula; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Ngamahu tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Ngamahu and is led by the chieftain Kaom; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Ramako tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Ramako and is led by the chieftain Ahuana; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Rongokurai tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Rongokurai and is led by the chieftain Kahuturoa; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Tasalio tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tasalio and is led by the chieftain Rakiata; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Tawhoa tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tawhoa and is led by the chieftain Maata; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Tukohama tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tukohama and is led by the chieftain Akoya; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Valako tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Valako and is led by the chieftain Kiloava; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Keepers of the Flame (Order of the Purple Flame)
nodes.summary: Monastic order founded by Ailith after her visions of the Dreamer; they train in the Monastery to defend Wraeclast against the Hiveborn and tend the Genesis Tree. The PoE2 wiki calls it the Order of the Purple Flame; the Monk class belongs to it. It is a taboo among them to speak the Dreamer's true name (Chayula).
sources: Visit the Monastery of the Keepers: "Welcome to our Monastery..."

alt_summaries.summary: Cult formed in Chayula's dreams, dedicated to destroying the Hiveborn; based at the Monastery of the Keepers.

nodes.name: Knights of the Sun
nodes.summary: Warriors and military enforcers under direct orders of the King, led by Olroth.

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran martial order led by Olroth who adopted gems on weapons and armour.
Powerful Kalguuran warriors/enforcers directly under the King; led by Olroth; religious scrutiny by them drove some emigration.

nodes.name: The Lightless
nodes.summary: Necromantic army of possessed golems created by Kulemak, led by Abyssal Liches; ended the primeval civilisation.

nodes.name: The Maji
nodes.summary: Azmeri vanguard chosen when the Wildwood was made; they purge the Nameless and fight the King in the Mists, forbidden from touching virtue gems ('Tears of the Maji').

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri vanguard sent into the Wildwood to wait while it is purged of evil, waging war on the King in the Mists.

nodes.name: Maraketh
nodes.summary: Desert people of the Vastiri led by Sekhemas, living in akhara (tribes). In 1333 IC Sekhema Deshret joined the Purity Rebellion in exchange for the return of the Vastiri Plains; later, Deshret sealed the Highgate mines. A large tribe lives at Highgate in PoE1; the Ardura akhara and Sekhema Asala appear in PoE2.

alt_summaries.summary: Matriarchal people led by sekhema, ancient dwellers of Vastiri for 304 generations; endured the Winter of the World, expelled the Lightless, had a thousand-year golden age at Keth, then lost their gods to the Beast's slumber and drifted into the desert.
Desert nomads of the Vastiri.
Desert people of the Vastiri; the Ardura akhara and the honoured dead of Deshar are Maraketh.

nodes.name: Meridian Free Traders
nodes.summary: Trade guild that sent Raulf to assist executing the Kingsmarch charter; in PoE2 it controls boat charters (Makoru captains the Aurora May under it).

alt_summaries.summary: Kingsmarch guild under which Makoru's Aurora May works; requires an account and charter from Rog.

nodes.name: Mutewind (warband)
nodes.summary: One of the three Warbands in Warbands league, alongside Brinerot and Redblades; the wiki calls them the Peak-dwellers. Their outcast Qianga delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay for the Order of the Djinn. Mutewind Warbands also appear as bosses in the Delve map Frozen Hollow.
sources: Warbands item list: Mutewind Wildrunner, Mutewind Lynx, Mutewind Seal
Qianga entry: 'a Mutewind warband outcast'; 'The Mutewind|Peak-dwellers'

nodes.name: House Grattus (Necropolis dead)
nodes.summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'Grattus Signet'.

nodes.name: House Nevalius (Necropolis dead)
nodes.summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'Nevalius Inheritance'.

nodes.name: House Perandus (Necropolis dead)
nodes.summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Perandus Pact'.

nodes.name: House Phrecia (Necropolis dead)
nodes.summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Hand of Phrecia'.

nodes.name: House Veruso (Necropolis dead)
nodes.summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'Veruso's Ambition'.

nodes.name: Priests of the Chalice
nodes.summary: Religious order that read the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes.

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran priesthood led by Uhtred; found the ancient artefact at the shrine.
Kalguuran priesthood (Priests of the Chalice) that interpreted the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes; Uhtred was its High Priest.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Secret society founded in ancient times by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper (Ahkeli) that protects Wraeclast from calamity and guards dangerous artefacts (Forbidden Vaults near the Oasis, Act 9); takes one orphan from each culture. Members forged and delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay (video). Janus Perandus's betrayal let Catarina raid the vault and the Order was slain except Jun and Janus; in PoE2 Jun is rebuilding it. Past members include Ixchel (later the Trialmaster).
sources: 1:07 order of the Djinn; 16:34 Starforge; 20:10 infiltration of Forbidden Vault

alt_summaries.summary: Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamity and guard dangerous artefacts. Icius Perandus and, much later, Janus Perandus belonged to it.
Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamities; Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.

Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper that guards dangerous artefacts and prevents calamities; selects one orphan from each culture. Members include Jun, Janus Perandus, Saresh, Ixchel, Dhunan, Sumei (investigated Kalandra's duplication of artefacts). Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.
Secret order (Jado's) replenishing its ranks; Jado confirms they infiltrated the Sel Khari and will be in Oriath.
Secret order founded by the Maraketh to guard relics and protect Wraeclast; nearly destroyed by Janus's betrayal in PoE1's Betrayal; Jun rebuilds it in secret, per PoE2.

nodes.name: The Pale Council
nodes.summary: Group of four Pale Court bosses (Yriel, Eber, Volkuur and Inya) fought through the Prophecy system; the wiki says the Pale Council fight no longer exists after 3.17.0. In the wiki's in-world history the Pale Council were rulers of an unidentified people, likely the Karui.
sources: section 'The Pale Council': '[[The Pale Council]] is a group comprising of Yriel, the Feral Lord, Eber, the Plaguemaw, Volkuur, and Inya'
Drops: 'sequence of last alive member of the Pale Council is random'; Version history 3.0.0 'The Pale Council encounter has been rebalanced'
Header: 'The Pale Council fight no longer exists in Path of Exile'

nodes.name: Perandus family
nodes.summary: Wealthiest merchant-lender family of the Eternal Empire (motto 'With piety and justice'). Blocked from the throne by the Phrecians, they rigged Izaro's Labyrinth so Chitus Perandus won; Cadiro looted the treasury before the fall. Descendants include Syndicate member Janus Perandus.
sources: forum announcement describing Cadiro's stolen treasury and indebted dead

alt_summaries.summary: Wealthy and powerful Eternal Empire family that put Malachai in place; basis for the Perandus league treasures.

nodes.name: Phrecian dynasty
nodes.summary: Unbroken line of emperors descended from Alano Phrecia, who founded the line after killing the 'dark being' in 35 IC. It ran from Alano through Romira and Tyndarus to Izaro, who was childless.
sources: sections 'Reign of Alano Phrecia' to 'Reign of Izaro'

nodes.name: Precursors
nodes.summary: Technologically superior ancient civilisation that wholly predates the Winter of the World; mastered corruption, built the Towers (terraforming), the Precursor Weapon and the Arbiter of Ash, then triggered cataclysms of fire, eruptions and sky-impacts. Pictographs read 'Death lies within'.

chronology.relative: further before the Vaal than the Vaal are before the present

nodes.name: Primeval Civilization ("Proto-Vaal")
nodes.summary: Ancient civilisation preceding the Vaal, unearthed in the Azurite Mine; the name "Proto-Vaal" is an internal term never used in-game and no link to the Vaal is established.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient culture (internally called 'Proto-Vaal') buried beneath Vaal and Lightless ruins in the Azurite Mines, known from glyphs; First King Uzaza, tyrant Putembo, last king Aul. No proven link to the Vaal.

nodes.name: Purity Rebellion
nodes.summary: Coalition led by High Templar Voll of Thebrus against Chitus' gem-and-thaumaturgy 'thaumatocracy'. Its supporters included Victario, Ondar, Geofri, Kastov and Adus, with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh allies.

nodes.name: Redblades
nodes.summary: Human tribe descended from those who settled the Titans' volcanoes; they ritually sacrifice humans to the Molten One, possibly because a Titan destroyed an outpost of El'Abin.

nodes.name: Remembrancers
nodes.summary: Kalguuran scribes who documented the explorations; the Prime Remembrancer's logbooks tell the expedition's fall.

alt_summaries.summary: Documentarians of Kalguuran explorations.

nodes.name: Runefathers
nodes.summary: Aldur's chosen apprentices and artisans of runesmithing; forged the Triskelion Flame to reunite fractured Middengard.
sources: ===The Triskelion Flame===: "After Aldur had passed away, the Runefathers gathered to forge the Triskelion Flame."

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran runesmiths who gathered after Aldur's death to forge the Triskelion Flame in his honour.

nodes.name: Karui Slave Rebellion
nodes.summary: Rebellion of enslaved Karui in Oriath led by Utula.

nodes.name: Order of the Templar
nodes.summary: Theocratic order led by a High Templar that worships Innocence. Within the Eternal Empire it produced figures such as High Templars Andronicus and Voll; after the Cataclysm it governed the unaffected island of Oriath as the Templar Theocracy, with Dominus and Avarius as its PoE1-era High Templars.

alt_summaries.summary: A human faction led by a High Templar, governing the theocracy of Oriath in the name of Innocence. Its members include High Templars Dominus, Voll and Avarius.
Theocratic order ruling Oriath.

nodes.name: The Crimson Scribe
nodes.summary: Society named as the client on Heist contracts targeting the Seal of Solaris, Seal of Lunaris, Ez Myrae Tome, Staff of the First Sin Eater and Golden Ibis; its targets indicate interest in the Winter of the World and the primeval civilization.

nodes.name: The Ring
nodes.summary: Rogue guild that runs the Rogue Harbour and fulfils Heist contracts for clients such as Administrator Qotra and the Crimson Scribe. The Count Geonor passage in the wiki says he contracted the Ring. Its leader is referred to only as 'the Boss'.

nodes.name: The Unblinking Eye
nodes.summary: Mysterious group associated with the Templars involved in notable events in Wraeclast's history.

nodes.name: The Three Sisters
nodes.summary: Cross-cultural myth of the sun, moon and earth sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and ended the Winter of the World; named differently by Eternals, Maraketh, Karui, Azmeri and the Wildwood Draiocht (Catha, Mhacha, Morrigan).

alt_summaries.summary: Sun, Moon (and Earth) sisters/gods named differently per culture who ended the Winter of the World by destroying Kulemak's mortal form. Minimal node; owned by another domain.

nodes.name: Trarthans
nodes.summary: People of Trarthus descended from Eternal Empire exiles and slaves, led by four Great Houses.

nodes.name: The Vaal
nodes.summary: Oldest identified civilisation of Wraeclast and in its heyday its most powerful nation; first known users of virtue gems, practitioners of mass blood sacrifice and slavery. All but 3,126 died in the Vaal Cataclysm; survivors assimilated into the Azmeri.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient Vaal civilisation.
Vaal civilisation of Utzaal and its remnants; Alva is a descendant of Vaal survivors.

nodes.name: The Royal Architects of Atzoatl
nodes.summary: Group of Vaal architects serving Atziri who built the Temple; Incursion has Vaal Architect mini-bosses. PoE2 Medallion flavour names Architects of the Guild, Vault, Destruction, Hoard, Forge and Nexus and associates Quipolatl, Puhuarte, Juatalotli, Hayoxi, Estazunti with them.

nodes.name: Vaal survivors / Savage tribes heirs
nodes.summary: The 3,126 survivors who merged into Azmeri tribes; later Azmeri/Karui cultures inherit Vaal remnants. Descendants of Vaal blood persist (e.g. Alva Valai; the Cuachic).
sources: Doryani: 'a living descendant of our people'

nodes.name: Vox family
nodes.summary: Oriathan nobility that became a criminal enterprise; the wiki describes the twins Vic and Vinny Vox using coercion, blackmail and violence to hold a place at the centre of Oriath business and social life. Descended from Cardinal Sanctus Vox.

nodes.name: Warbands (Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind)
nodes.summary: Three roaming warring clans of Warbands league (2.0.0) with leaders and elites: Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind; members Korell Goya, Guff Grenn, Rin Yuushu later joined the Syndicate.

nodes.name: Watchers of Decay
nodes.summary: Ancient organisation of parents founded when a nameless god told an Azmeri mother whose child was stolen about the Elder. They forged Starforge to subdue it by separating form and spirit. Their Map Device (Book of Memories p9) later became the Atlas device. Associated with the Order of the Djinn on the wiki; membership of Egrin/Qianga/Betucia is unclear.

nodes.name: Abyss league
nodes.summary: Abyss league Launched 2017-12-08 (version 3.1.0). Abysses are cracks and pits spawning monsters; introduces abyss jewels, Stygian Vises, Abyssal Depths and Abyssal Liches.

nodes.name: Affliction league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.23.0 (8 Dec 2023 - 26 Mar 2024): the player cleanses the Affliction of the Viridian Wildwood with sacred wisps, trains with the Azmeri and unlocks Wildwood ascendancy classes; the King in the Mists is the antagonist.

nodes.name: Allflame league (Curse of the Allflame)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.29.0 (24 Jul 2026; announced end 9 Nov 2026): aboard Valerie's ship the Sovereign, Exiles chart the Fathomless Depths with Allflame lanterns and craft with Vesper.

nodes.name: Ambush league
nodes.summary: Ambush league launched 2014-03-05 (1.1.0, Sacrifice of the Vaal); introduced Strongboxes. Ran with hardcore Invasion league.

nodes.name: Anarchy league
nodes.summary: Anarchy league launched 2013-06-07 (0.11.0); introduced rogue exiles and league challenges. Hardcore twin: Onslaught.

nodes.name: Ancestor league (Trial of the Ancestors)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.22.0 (18 Aug - 5 Dec 2023): Exiles use Silver Coins to enter the Karui afterlife and field a team of Karui warriors in the Trial of the Ancestors tournament against fallen chieftains, under Hinekora.

nodes.name: Archnemesis league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which petrified monsters are imbued with itemised Archnemesis modifiers to build custom rare boss fights. Mechanics-driven; no dedicated narrative NPC in the wiki corpus.

nodes.name: Bestiary league
nodes.summary: Bestiary league Launched 2018-03-02 (version 3.2.0). Einhar Frey teaches the Exile to capture beasts with nets, for beastcrafting and to challenge the Spirit Beasts (the First Ones).

nodes.name: Betrayal league
nodes.summary: Betrayal league Launched 2018-12-07 (version 3.5.0). Jun Ortoi leads the hunt for the Immortal Syndicate, which has taken the forsaken masters; revamps the master system.

nodes.name: Beyond league
nodes.summary: Beyond league launched 2014-08-20 (1.2.0, Forsaken Masters): extradimensional demons invade via portals that grow with nearby kills, culminating in a unique boss. Hardcore twin of Rampage.

nodes.name: Blight league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which Sister Cassia asks the exile to defend a Purification Pump against fungal Blight growths; rewards Oils used to Anoint items.

nodes.name: Bloodlines league
nodes.summary: Bloodlines league Launched 2014-12-13 (version 1.3.0). Hardcore twin of Torment; Bloodline-empowered monsters with special modifiers. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Breach league
nodes.summary: Breach league Launched 2016-12-02 (version 2.5.0). Breaches open parallel realms of otherworldly monsters; splinters form Breachstones to challenge the five Breachlords in their domains.

nodes.name: Crucible league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.21.0 (7 Apr - 15 Aug 2023, 'Path of Exile: Crucible'): Crucible Forges grant equipment a passive tree, and Primeval Remnants open portals to the Forge of the Titans.

nodes.name: Delirium league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which Mirrors of Delirium in each area release a spreading fog of madness; leads to the Simulacrum and Cluster Jewels.

nodes.name: Delve league
nodes.summary: Delve league Launched 2018-08-31 (version 3.4.0). Niko the Mad guides the Exile into the infinite Azurite Mine beneath Wraeclast, powered by Voltaxic Sulphite.

nodes.name: Domination league
nodes.summary: Domination league launched 2013-10-23 (1.0.0, Path of Exile release); introduced Shrines. Hardcore twin: Nemesis.

nodes.name: Echoes of the Atlas (3.13.0)
nodes.summary: League/expansion that introduced the Maven and the Envoy.

nodes.name: Essence league
nodes.summary: Essence league launched 2016-09-02 (2.4.0, Atlas of Worlds): frozen monsters hold an Essence; freeing them grants it. Essences give guaranteed affixes and can be corrupted.

nodes.name: Expedition league
nodes.summary: Challenge league introducing four Kalguuran expedition NPCs (Gwennen, Tujen, Rog, Dannig) who excavate the lost settlements of their ancestors with explosives. The Kalguur are referenced again in Settlers (Kingsmarch) and in PoE2.

nodes.name: Harbinger league
nodes.summary: Harbinger league launched 2017-08-04 (3.0.0, The Fall of Oriath): otherworldly Harbingers, defeated by destroying their minions, drop shards of currency.

nodes.name: Harvest league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the Azmeri outcast Oshabi has the exile plant seeds in the Sacred Grove and harvest Lifeforce for crafting; ends with the Avatar of the Grove boss. Later reworked into a core mechanic.

nodes.name: Heist league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the exile uses Rogue's Markers to enter the Rogue Harbour, run Contracts for the Ring, and hire rogues to steal valuables from fortified caches (Contracts, Blueprints, Grand Heists).

nodes.name: Incursion league
nodes.summary: PoE1 3.3.0 challenge league (June 2018) in which Alva Valai opens incursions 2,000 years into the past to the Temple of Atzoatl; later became a core Master mechanic.

nodes.name: Invasion league
nodes.summary: Invasion league Launched 2014-03-05 (version 1.1.0). Hardcore twin of Ambush; invasion bosses spawn in areas. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Lake of Kalandra league
aliases: Path of Exile: Lake of Kalandra
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the player assembles a Mirrored Tablet of reflected encounters and enters the Lake of Kalandra, meeting the ancient trapped entity Kalandra.

chronology.relative: 3.19.0 'Path of Exile: Lake of Kalandra', 2022-08-19 to 2022-12-06

alt_summaries.summary: Challenge league released 19 Aug 2022 in version 3.19.0 (ended 6 Dec 2022): Mirrored Tablets let players build reflected encounters in the Lake of Kalandra.

nodes.name: Keepers of the Flame league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.27.0 (31 Oct 2025 - 2 Mar 2026): the Exile works with Ailith to repel Hiveborn invading via stabilised Breach connections and grows the Genesis Tree; Breach joined the core game in 3.28.0.
sources: lead; Into the Breach version history

alt_summaries.summary: PoE1 league (3.27.0) that introduced the new Breach (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree); the mechanic became core in 3.28.0 replacing the original Breach. Minimal node; full release data owned by another domain.

nodes.name: Legion league
nodes.summary: Legion league Launched 2019-06-07 (version 3.7.0). Timeless Monoliths reveal legions frozen mid-battle; Emblems open the Domain of Timeless Conflict. Legion mechanic reworked in 3.29 per wiki (incubators no longer drop).

nodes.name: Mercenaries league (Mercenaries of Trarthus)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.26.0 (13 Jun - 27 Oct 2025): lawless Trarthan veterans can be fought and hired; noble mercenaries descend from the four death-trade Great Houses.

nodes.name: Metamorph league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the alchemist Tane Octavius has the exile gather organs from monsters to build shape-changing Metamorphs; introduces Catalysts.

nodes.name: Mirage league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.28.0 (6 Mar 2026; scheduled to end 20 Jul 2026): with Sekhema Varashta the Exile frees djinn tortured by the Afarud via mirages and the astral realm; endgame necromancer Saresh.

nodes.name: Necro Settlers event
nodes.summary: Event run Nov 2024 - Feb 2025 during the extended Settlers league, combining Necropolis content with Settlers.
sources: intro: 'Necro Settlers event was held from November 2024 to February 2025'

nodes.name: Necropolis league
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.24.0 (29 Mar - 23 Jul 2024): Undertaker Arimor lends the Exile his Lantern to haunt monsters, collect their corpses and bury them in the Necropolis for grave crafting; Embers of the Allflame transform monsters.

nodes.name: Nemesis league
nodes.summary: Nemesis league launched 2013-10-23 (1.0.0); every rare monster has a Nemesis modifier. Standard twin: Domination.

nodes.name: Onslaught league
nodes.summary: Onslaught league launched 2013-06-07 (0.11.0); monsters have 20% increased movement and attack speed. Standard twin: Anarchy.

nodes.name: Perandus league
nodes.summary: Perandus league launched 2016-03-04 (2.2.0, Ascendancy): after the Cataclysm Cadiro Perandus hid family treasures in caches across Wraeclast; players open guarded caches and trade Perandus Coins with Cadiro.

nodes.name: Legacy of Phrecia
nodes.summary: 'Legacy of Phrecia': a limited returning PoE1 event (ascendancy/idol rework). First run ended 23 Apr 2025; it returned during the 3.27 (Keepers of the Flame) cycle from 29 Jan 2026 for about 20 days, per third-party news. Its lore link to the ancient Phrecian/imperial-heartland history is by name only (unverified).

chronology.relative: first run ended Apr 2025; 3.27-cycle rerun 29 Jan - 19 Feb 2026 (third-party news)

sources: article on the end of the event (23 Apr 2025)
official event page (not re-fetched by checker)

alt_summaries.summary: Event (run after the Necro Settlers event until 23 April 2025, with a second run later adding random modifiers) that replaces the 19 ascendancy classes with alternate 'whacky ideas' classes and replaces the Atlas passive tree with an idol system.

nodes.name: Forbidden Rites league (PoE2)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access event league (0.5.5, 2026-09-04) built on Ritual altars in campaign and endgame zones, with unique-boss Ritual clusters per act and Sacred Bloom Wildwood encounters; 0.5.5 also integrates Runes of Aldur and Expedition into the core PoE2 game.
sources: lead, 'League content' and unique boss rituals

alt_summaries.summary: 0.5.5 event league (2026-09-04) running beside Runes of Aldur: Ritual encounters in every campaign and endgame zone, unique-boss Ritual clusters per act, Viridian Wildwood via Sacred Bloom; integrates Runes of Aldur and Expedition into core.

nodes.name: Rise of the Abyssal
nodes.summary: First 'full' PoE2 league (0.3.0, 2025-08-29 to 2025-12-09): Abyssal fissures open as green cracks near monster packs; closing them reveals an Abyssal Trove and sometimes the Abyssal Depths; preserved bones feed desecration at the Well of Souls (Act 2).

alt_summaries.summary: Challenge league launched 2025-08-29 with The Third Edict (v0.3.0), the release that added Act 4, the Interludes and Abyss content.
First PoE2 full league, launched 2025-08-29 with version 0.3.0 (The Third Edict); Abysses, preserved bones, the Well of Souls (Act 2) and desecrated modifiers.

nodes.name: Runes of Aldur
nodes.summary: 0.5.0 temporary league: Farrow studies runes on Verisium Remnants (Ezomyte Runesmithing with Kalguuran origins), producing Runic Ward, Kalguuran gems and alloys; folded into the core game with Expedition in 0.5.5.
sources: Runes of Aldur (Runesmithing): Farrow, a young blacksmith, reveals the Kalguuran origins of Ezomyte Runesmithing

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 Early Access temporary league (0.5.0 'Return of the Ancients', 2026-05-29) in which Farrow studies runes on Verisium Remnants; brings Kalguuran runesmithing, Ward and Kalguuran gems to PoE2.

nodes.name: Prophecy league
nodes.summary: Prophecy league launched 2016-06-03 (2.3.0): silver coins traded with Navali for prophecies; the Pale Council league bosses of the Pale Court were tied to prophecies.

nodes.name: Rampage league
nodes.summary: Rampage league Launched 2014-08-20 (version 1.2.0). Kill-streak mechanic (paired with Beyond), part of Forsaken Masters. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Ritual league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which a Ritual Altar in each zone starts a wave fight that awards Tribute, spendable on a shop of pre-identified items. Narrative content is minimal in PoE1; the same Ritual altar mechanic returns in PoE2's Forbidden Rites league (0.5.5).

nodes.name: Sacrifice of the Vaal
nodes.summary: PoE1 1.1.0 mini-expansion centred on Atziri and Vaal side areas.

nodes.name: Sanctum league (The Forbidden Sanctum)
nodes.summary: PoE1 challenge league 3.20.0 (9 Dec 2022 - 4 Apr 2023; shipped as 'Path of Exile: The Forbidden Sanctum'): a roguelite run through an ancient Templar enclave beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, controlled by a malevolent entity (Lycia is its fourth-floor boss).

nodes.name: Scourge league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which The Last to Die gives the exile a Blood Crucible to corrupt items while fighting through a demon-ridden 'Nightmare' mirror of Wraeclast; its monsters became the new Beyond monsters.

nodes.name: Path of Exile: Secrets of the Atlas
nodes.summary: PoE1 expansion 3.26.0 (13 Jun 2025) containing Mercenaries league and the Originator endgame storyline (Zana the Originator, Eagon Caeserius, Threads of the Originator); Settlers' Kingsmarch services were added to the core game.
sources: release 2025-06-13, 'Path of Exile: Secrets of the Atlas' 3.26.0

alt_summaries.summary: Expansion launched 13 June 2025 (3.26.0, with Mercenaries league) adding Eagon, Zana the Originator, Memory Tears and the Incarnations; 3.28.0 reworked the Atlas.

nodes.name: Sentinel league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which Sentinel drones empower monsters; Power Cores charge Sentinel filaments and Recombinators combine two equipment items. Sentinel mechanics were added to the core game in 3.25; existing Recombinators remained usable.

nodes.name: Settlers of Kalguur league
nodes.summary: PoE1 expansion/league 3.25.0 (26 Jul 2024; league ended 9 Jun 2025 22:00 UTC / 10 Jun 2025 00:00 GMT+2 per GGG after multiple extensions for PoE2 Early Access, over 45 weeks): the Exile helps Kalguuran settlers build Kingsmarch, a harbour meant to facilitate trade between the settlers, the Karui archipelago and Kalguur. Town-building ended in 3.26.0; Kingsmarch services joined the core game.
sources: GGG forum "What Will Happen When The Settlers League Ends": "The league will end on Jun 10, 2025 12:00 AM (GMT+2)"; "Kingsmarch will be going core in 3.26"

nodes.name: Siege of the Atlas (3.17.0)
nodes.summary: Expansion that added the Searing Exarch, Eater of Worlds and the Eldritch system.

nodes.name: Synthesis league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which fragments of lost memories are scattered through Wraeclast; the player stabilises them and links them in the Memory Nexus. Guide NPC Cavas turns out to be the High Templar Venarius. Not added to the core game; its bosses (Synthetes, Venarius) survive as unique maps.

alt_summaries.summary: 3.6.0 challenge league (Mar 2019) centred on Cavas and decaying memories; bosses later became unique map content and Kirac missions.

nodes.name: Talisman league
nodes.summary: Talisman league launched 2015-12-11 (version 2.1.0). Monsters are possessed by ancient Ezomyte Talismans; killing them yields the Talisman. Boss: Rigwald, the Wolven King.

nodes.name: Tempest league
nodes.summary: Tempest league launched 2015-07-10 (2.0.0, The Awakening); hardcore sibling of Warbands that introduced Tempests, area modifiers that alter monsters and players (size, damage, drops).

nodes.name: Torment league
nodes.summary: Torment league launched 2014-12-13 (1.3.0): spirits of tormented criminals haunt areas, flee when met, imbue monsters and yield their ill-gotten gains when slain. Hardcore twin: Bloodlines.

nodes.name: Ultimatum league
nodes.summary: Vaal-themed challenge league in which the Trialmaster, servant of the entity Chaos, offers escalating Trials of Chaos for the player to risk or bank rewards. Re-integrated into the core game in 3.23.0.

nodes.name: Warbands league
nodes.summary: Warbands league Launched 2015-07-10 (version 2.0.0). Warring clans (Redblade, Brinerot, Mutewind) roam Wraeclast in synergistic groups with leaders and elites. (Mechanic detail abbreviated; release data from wiki.)

nodes.name: Absence of Mercy and Empathy
nodes.summary: The Maven's realm in the Atlas; entering it with a The Maven's Writ starts The Maven's Game epilogue quest and hosts the Maven pinnacle fight.
sources: intro paragraph: 'This quest will automatically be obtained after entering Absence of Mercy and Empathy using a The Maven's Writ'

nodes.name: Absence of Patience and Wisdom
nodes.summary: Atlas map realm where The Searing Exarch is fought in the Searing Exarch epilogue quest.
sources: Quest log: 'Enter The Absence of Patience and Wisdom'

nodes.name: Absence of Symmetry and Harmony
nodes.summary: Atlas map realm where The Eater of Worlds is fought in the Eater of Worlds epilogue quest.
sources: Quest log: 'Enter Absence of Symmetry and Harmony'

nodes.name: Absence of Value and Meaning
nodes.summary: Elder's arena in the Atlas.
sources: 'defeat The Elder in Absence of Value and Meaning'

nodes.name: Abyssal Depths
nodes.summary: Areas reached from Abysses containing Abyssal monsters and lich bosses Amanamu and Ulaman.

nodes.name: Abyssal Depths (Delve)
nodes.summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) that uses Abyss theme and contains Abyss monsters. It is distinct from the Abyssal City biome (which spawns The Lich's Tomb) and from the Abyssal Depths map area (existing node loc_abyssal_depths).
sources: Intro: 'Abyssal Depths is a biome within the Azurite Mine'; hatnote: 'For the area accessible from completing an Abyss encounter in map'; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game.'

nodes.name: The Alluring Abyss
nodes.summary: PoE1 area for Uber Atziri (Mortal fragments).

nodes.name: The Ancient Pyramid (PoE1 Act 2)
nodes.summary: Vaal pyramid in Act 2 housing the Dark Altar where the Vaal Oversoul is fought.

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal pyramid in the Caverns beyond the Vaal Ruins with the Dark Altar.

nodes.name: The Apex of Sacrifice
nodes.summary: PoE1 map-device area (Sacrifice fragments) in which Atziri is fought.

nodes.name: Atlas of Worlds
nodes.summary: The dreamlike plane of interlinked worlds at the centre of PoE1's endgame; its mists reflect the desires of whoever walks it (Veritania's journal). Time there is 'a mirage' (Baran). Reached via the Map Device.
sources: Journal I: 'There is only my will, my thoughts, and my expectations, reflected as countless echoes'
Journal III: 'Time in the Atlas is a mirage'

nodes.name: Atziri's Temple (Lira Vaal)
nodes.summary: Past version of the temple unlocked via Ancient Beacons; the present ruin is the Lost Temple. Built via the Temple Console; Doryani turns the entrance into a time portal after Act 3/4.
sources: lead; Ancient Beacon; Doryani will activate the time portal

nodes.name: Aul's Domain (Crystal King's Throne)
nodes.summary: Delve area (internally 'Proto-Vaal city') of the Azurite Mine where the crystal-encased citadel and throne of Aul, the Crystal King, lie.
sources: Primeval civilization; footnote: 'Proto-Vaal' is the internal name of Delve's Primeval Chamber and The Crystal King's Throne

alt_summaries.summary: Delve node (Primeval Ruins biome) containing the Primeval Citadel where Aul is fought.

nodes.name: Axiom Prison
nodes.summary: Ancient clifftop prison (no one remembers who built it) used by every power that ruled Wraeclast; its warden Brutus was mutated; Act 1 area from Lower Prison to Warden's Chambers.
sources: Shavronne in her tower in the Prison

alt_summaries.summary: Eternal outpost warded by Brutus where Shavronne of Umbra experimented on him; blocked Karui advance.
Prison complex reached through the Act 6 Ridge; contains Shavronne's Tower, where Shavronne's spirit is killed for Sin.

nodes.name: Azala Vaal
nodes.summary: Vaal capital named after the burning of Lira Vaal's temple; now buried beneath Sarn where the Azmeri founded the Eternal Empire's capital.

alt_summaries.summary: Former capital of the Vaal Empire; Tarcus Veruso planted his banner here to found Sarn and the Eternal Empire.

nodes.name: Viridian Wildwood
nodes.summary: Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons there, the Maji fight the Nameless and the King in the Mists. PoE2 Last of the Druids setting.
sources: The Winter of the World > The Viridian Wildwood
paragraph on the forest not existing until 3.23.0

alt_summaries.summary: Haven created by the Draiocht as refuge from the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons; haunted by shadowy creatures such as the King in the Mists; home of the Maji.

Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World, where time loops in seasons. Contested by the Nameless and the King in the Mists; Chaos believes the forest did not exist until the 3.23 timeline.
Wildwood encounter on the Atlas, connected to Sacred Bloom rewards; Aoife is bound here.

nodes.name: Azmerian Ranges
nodes.summary: Mountain homeland of the ancient Azmeri; origin of the migrants who founded Sarn and the Eternal Empire, and where the Vaal first met the Azmeri.

nodes.name: The Azurite Mine
nodes.summary: Infinitely scaling dungeon beneath Wraeclast reached from the Mine Encampment; contains Primeval ruins, Vaal city, abyssal city biomes and darkness.

nodes.name: The Belly of the Beast
nodes.summary: Interior of the Beast with the Black Core.

nodes.name: The Brine King's Reef
nodes.summary: Blood-reef boss area at the end of Act 6, reached by Weylam Roth's ship the Black Crest, summoned with the Black Flag at the Beacon.

nodes.name: The Cathedral Rooftop (Act 10)
nodes.summary: Rooftop where Bannon holds off Kitava's cultists.

alt_summaries.summary: Where the Sign of Purity is used against Kitava.

nodes.name: Cemetery of the Eternals
nodes.summary: PoE2 Act 1 area in Ogham where Eternal praetors are entombed, with inscriptions claiming the land 'in life and death'.

alt_summaries.summary: Act 1 graveyard hosting the Tomb of the Consort and the Mausoleum of the Praetor.

nodes.name: Chamber of Innocence
nodes.summary: Templar chamber in Oriath built under High Templar Avarius whose stained glass windows tell the Sin and Innocence story.

alt_summaries.summary: Chamber where Avarius becomes Innocence.

nodes.name: Chamber of Sins
nodes.summary: Laboratory built by Chitus where Maligaro conducted flesh experiments, opposed by nearby Phrecia Cathedral; named by Archbishop Geofri.

alt_summaries.summary: Old Empire site where Maligaro worked; holds the Baleful Gem.
Inquisitor Maligaro's laboratory in Phrecia, with a secret passage to the Den.

nodes.name: The Control Blocks
nodes.summary: Templar prison blocks in Oriath.

nodes.name: The Crystal Veins
nodes.summary: Highgate caverns holding the Rapture Device, which the exile reactivates to enter the Beast.

alt_summaries.summary: Cave where the Rapture Device stands.

nodes.name: Mines (Delve)
nodes.summary: Biome of the Azurite Mine (Delve) that generates only at the top levels of the mine; contains Metallic, Serrated, Pristine and Aetheric fossils. Introduced in 3.4.0.
sources: Intro: 'Mines is one of the biomes of the Azurite Mine. It only generates at the very top levels of the mine'; Version history 3.4.0 'Introduced to the game'

nodes.name: Doedre's Cesspool
nodes.summary: Sewer area of the Toxic Conduits in Sarn where Doedre is killed in the Cauldron.
sources: Doedre's Cesspool contains The Cauldron boss arena

nodes.name: Domain of Timeless Conflict
nodes.summary: Area opened by combining Emblems in the map device; heart of the timeless conflict between legions.

nodes.name: The Ebony Barracks
nodes.summary: Blackguard base across the river in Sarn.

nodes.name: Eternal Laboratory
nodes.summary: Malachai's laboratory of the Eternal Empire, built on the archbishop Lazhwar's thaumaturgy research into maps; Zana's hideout alternative in the legacy Atlas quests.
sources: Eternal Empire section: 'Lazhwar... discovered maps to create the Eternal Laboratory'
Assignment: 'Talk to Zana in your Hideout or the Eternal Laboratory'

nodes.name: Eye of Hinekora / Halls of the Dead
nodes.summary: Karui afterlife realm unlocked by rescuing Matiki: Tests of Mettle for Kaom, Maata and Rakiata, the Halls of the Dead with Yama's trial and the audience with Hinekora.

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 Act 4 area accessible after rescuing Matiki; gateway to the Halls of the Dead and Trial of the Ancestors.

nodes.name: Ezomyr
nodes.summary: Ezomyte homeland on a landmass west of the Wraeclastian mainland (with the Isles of Skothe), later largely wiped out by a plague; Ogham forests in PoE2 Act 1.

nodes.name: The Fathomless Depths
nodes.summary: Underwater endgame area explored via a Bathysphere and Allflame lanterns; a pit of deathly light lies below.

nodes.name: Fellshrine Ruins
nodes.summary: Ruined former Freesia Cathedral area of Wraeclast, above the Forbidden Sanctum; Eramir calls the Fellshrine a shadow of what was once good in Wraeclast.

nodes.name: The Forbidden Sanctum
nodes.summary: Ancient Templar enclave/ossuary-library beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, four floors deep, abandoned for a long time and now controlled by Lycia, who lures treasure hunters in through portals; floors shift from tidy library to Scourge-infested crypt.
sources: '==Lore==': 'ancient Templar enclave hidden beneath the Fellshrine Ruins'
[4:05]-[4:30] four floors, library to crypt; [10:35]-[11:30] ossuary and pact

alt_summaries.summary: Templar catacombs under the Fellshrine Ruins (PoE1 Sanctum): lithomancy, necromancy and hidden truths of Innocence's ascension. Background for Oriathan Templar secrecy; no source ties it to the Twilight Order.

nodes.name: The Forest Encampment
nodes.summary: Former Azmeri/exile village taken over by Ralakesh through Greust; located between the Ashen Fields and the Northern Forest in Act 7.
sources: Ralakesh is located in The Forest Encampment

alt_summaries.summary: Act 2 town in the Phrecian forest, a village of Greust, Silk, Yeena, Eramir.

nodes.name: Forge of the Titans
nodes.summary: Primeval forge reached through Primeval Remnants during Crucible league, where equipment trees are combined; the stone body and voice of the Molten One, the last known Titan, can be met there.
sources: '==League Mechanic==' Primeval Remnant / Forge of the Titans
Molten One entry: 'During Crucible league, his stone body and voice can be encountered in the Forge of the Titans'

alt_summaries.summary: Volcanic caldera (Crucible league) where the Molten One dwells and the Redblades worship him.

nodes.name: The Grand Architect's Temple
nodes.summary: Delve node in the Vaal Outpost biome housing the boss Ahuatotli, the Blind.

nodes.name: The Halls of the Dead
nodes.summary: Karui afterlife created by Hinekora before the Slumbering of the Gods as a place for Karui souls; where fallen chieftains reside and the Trial of the Ancestors is held.
sources: '==Items==' (portal to the Halls of the Dead)

nodes.name: The High Gardens
nodes.summary: Act 8 gardens associated with Izaro, where Yugul lurks.

nodes.name: Highgate
nodes.summary: Mountain region where Veruso buried the virtue gems ('Tears of Maji'), where slaves mined them under Chitus, where Malachai placed the Rapture Device and the Beast lies beneath, and where a Maraketh tribe lives in PoE1.
sources: 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Slave trade', 'Reign of Voll'

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh-held mining settlement north of Sarn, Act 4 town.
Mining town built over the Beast's corpse; Act 9 town whose waters run red with the Beast's blood. Maraketh Irasha, Tasuni and relic hunters Petarus and Vanja live here.

nodes.name: Isles of Skothe
nodes.summary: Landmass west of Sarn named with Ezomyr as the origin of the Ezomytes.

nodes.name: Kalguur
nodes.summary: Homeland of the Kalguur people in Middengard, a distant continent southeast/east of Wraeclast; not directly accessible but referenced by Expedition and Settlers of Kalguur.

alt_summaries.summary: Homeland of the Kalguurans on the continent Middengard, south-east of Wraeclast; ruled by a mysterious King Cadigan who gives charters to successful outposts.

nodes.name: Kaom's Stronghold
nodes.summary: Karui stronghold within the Beast where Kaom is fought.

nodes.name: The Karui Fortress
nodes.summary: Act 6 area containing Tukohama's Keep, where the Karui war god is fought.

nodes.name: Karui Shores
nodes.summary: Epilogue hub leading to the Atlas of Worlds.
sources: Upon entering Karui Shores talk to Helena

nodes.name: Keth
nodes.summary: Ancient Maraketh city and trade empire at the meeting of seven rivers, called the 'glory of the world'; ruins form an Act 2 area in PoE2.
sources: Walkthrough 'Use the Desert Map to travel to Keth'

alt_summaries.summary: Buried city where the Water Goddess Halani lies and the Essence of Water is found.

nodes.name: Kingsmarch
nodes.summary: Kalguuran harbour town on Ngamakanui, hub of Act 4 where the Exile hires the Aurora May. Founded in PoE1's Settlers of Kalguur; Tujen says they first picked the spot to stash supplies and 'now it's going to be a city'. In the epilogue its ruins are revisited by Dannig and Makoru.
sources: intro + '==NPCs=='; Trivia 'Act 4 town in Path of Exile 2'

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran-chartered port and hub town on the Karui coast, reached via Johan in the Karui Shores (Epilogue). Run by the King's Hand under a Charter, it hosts Dannig, Tujen, Rog, Isla, Faustus, Raulf and Sonja. In PoE2 it is the Act 4 town and later lies in ruins in the endgame.

nodes.name: Korathin
nodes.summary: Capital of Trarthus, declared by Ixan Keita in 872 IC and built by his slaves.

nodes.name: Lake of Kalandra
nodes.summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars in primordial Wraeclast where Kalandra is trapped. The league version was a mirror-realm assembled from a Mirrored Tablet and was not added to the core game.
sources: League Mechanic and note on core game

alt_summaries.summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars that existed when 'nothing but the lake' did; Kalandra is trapped in it. The Kalandra league lets the Exile stage reflected encounters there.

nodes.name: The Lich's Tomb
nodes.summary: Delve node of the Azurite Mine, found in the Abyssal City biome at depth 90+; it always contains the boss fight with Kurgal, the Blackblooded in the Abyssal Sanctum. The boss room is no longer accessible in a new instance after the kill.
sources: Intro: 'It can only appeared in 90+ depths in the Abyssal City biome ... it always contains the boss fight with Kurgal, the Blackblooded'; 'After the boss fight has been finished, the node can be revisited'

nodes.name: Lioneye's Watch
nodes.summary: Southern Eternal garrison commanded by General Marceus Lioneye, taken by Kaom's Karui in the Purity Rebellion; later the survivors' town in PoE1 Acts 1 and 6.
sources: Lioneye's Watch is the Act 6 town
