edges.description: The Precursor civilisation, the only culture on Wraeclast to predate the Winter of the World, was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm.
sources: intro: 'an incredibly advanced precursor civilization existed, but was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm'; Precursor section: 'the only culture on Wraeclast to completely predate the Winter of the World'

edges.description: Uzaza is named as the First King of the primeval civilisation, whose rings tell of the civilisation's beginnings in a cold climate.
sources: section 'Notable members': '[[The First King]]'; section '"Uzaza's" rings'
section on Wraeclast's ancient civilisations: Atalui's research reveals that 'their "First King" was called Uzaza'

edges.description: Aul, the Crystal King, was the last king of the primeval civilisation.
sources: section 'Notable members': '[[Aul, the Crystal King]] (The Last King)'

edges.description: The primeval civilisation was ruled by a tyrant, Putembo, until the slave Aul overthrew him (per Atalui, quoted by the wiki; the Aul page instead says Aul served an unnamed king).
sources: Atalui's research (quoted in the Primeval civilization section): 'Aul overthrew a tyrant called Putembo'

edges.description: The primeval civilisation came to its end when Aul sealed his citadel in crystal in a final ritual.
sources: section 'Lore': 'came to its end when Aul performed a ritual that sealed his citadel in crystal'

edges.description: The primeval civilisation fell in the cataclysms that ended in Aul's crystal ritual.
sources: section 'Lore': 'came to its end when Aul performed a ritual'

edges.description: Alano Phrecia was crowned Emperor after defeating the dark being, founding the Phrecian line.
sources: Eternal Empire page, Phrecian succession (Alano Phrecia, founder of the line)

edges.description: Romira was a Phrecian ruler of the line descended from Alano Phrecia, deposed after Sarn burned.
sources: Eternal Empire page: 'Sarn was burned to the ground ... and Romira was desposed'

edges.description: Tyndarus Phrecius was an emperor of the Phrecian line, who lost the Trarthan war of independence.
sources: history section: 'Tyndarus tried to send reinforcements to Trarthus'

edges.description: Izaro was the last Phrecian emperor, who built the Lord's Labyrinth to choose a successor.
sources: Eternal Empire page, Phrecian succession (Izaro, last Phrecian emperor)

edges.description: Phrecian legions occupied Trarthus, and the Phrecian dynasty executed the Trarthan warlords.
sources: history section: 'The rebellion was escalated into a war led by four first-generation Trarthans'

edges.description: The Phrecian dynasty fought the Trarthan war of independence and lost Trarthus: after two years Tyndarus capitulated and withdrew his legions.
sources: history section: 'After two years, Tyndarus capitulated and withdrew his legions'

edges.description: Emperor Izaro opened the Lord's Labyrinth in 1317 IC to choose a successor.
sources: Eternal Empire page, Phrecian succession (Izaro built the Lord's Labyrinth)

edges.description: Criminals of Oriath were sentenced by the Templar Church for sins and shipped to Wraeclast as exiles.
sources: page 'Letters of Exile': charges and sentences, 1597-1599 IC

edges.description: The exiles of Wraeclast were sentenced by High Templar Dominus and shipped to Wraeclast.
sources: exile paragraph: 'The player character is one of many exiles who have received this sentence'

edges.description: Exiles were shipwrecked and washed up on the Twilight Strand.
sources: exile paragraph: 'Shipwrecked and washed up in the Twilight Strand'

edges.description: The Brinerot pirates worshipped the Brine King, whom the Exile killed at the reef in Act 6.
sources: quest page: the Brine King encounter at the reef (Act 6)
entry 'Tsoagoth, The Brine King': 'He is the god of the Brinerot pirates'

edges.description: The Black Scythe mercenaries led by Vorana were part of the expedition to Wraeclast, providing its defence.
sources: logbook quote 'The Omen I & The Journey I': '[[Vorana]], Mercenary leader of the Black Scythe'

edges.description: Ratha Azadi founded House Azadi, one of the four Great Houses of Trarthus.
sources: section on the Great Houses: House Azadi as the Trarthan assassin monopoly

edges.description: House Azadi, founded by Ratha Azadi, is one of the four Great Houses whose founders, the four first-generation Trarthans, led the rebellion against Phrecius.
sources: history section: 'four first-generation Trarthans, later known as the Great Founders'

edges.description: House Azadi took part in the Trarthan war of independence through its founder Ratha Azadi, one of the four Great Founders.
sources: history section: 'war led by four first-generation Trarthans, later known as the Great Founders'

edges.description: The Kitava tribe takes part in the Trial of the Ancestors, the ritual combat of the Karui Ancestors.
sources: section 'Afterlife': 'ritualistic combat in honor of the Ancestor'

edges.description: The Tasalio tribe takes part in the Trial of the Ancestors, the ritual combat of the Karui Ancestors.
sources: section 'Afterlife': 'ritualistic combat in honor of the Ancestor'

edges.description: The Knights of the Sun, led by Olroth, joined the first expedition to Wraeclast.
sources: logbook quote 'The Omen I & The Journey I': 'The trip was led by [[Olroth]], leader of the Knights of the Sun'

edges.description: The Citizen Vanguard, under Commander Kirac, commissioned the Exile to aid them on the Atlas.
sources: page 'A Call to Arms': the Exile is commissioned by Kirac to aid the Citizen Vanguard

edges.description: The Vaal Empire ended in the Vaal Cataclysm; only 3,126 Vaal survived, and they sought refuge with the Azmeri.
sources: section 'The Vaal Cataclysm': 'only 3,126 survived to seek refuge with the nearby Azmeri'

edges.description: The surviving Vaal sought refuge with the Azmeri and over time assimilated into the Azmeri population until no Vaal remained.
sources: section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' aftermath: 'Over time, they assimilated into the Azmeri population until no Vaal remained'

edges.description: The Maraketh tradition credits the twin Sekhemas Solerai and Lundara with ending the Winter of the World, the first recorded Maraketh war.
sources: section 'History': 'The Winter of the World is the first event in recorded Maraketh history'

edges.description: Surviving Maraketh join the Clayshaper Ahkeli to found the Order of the Djinn against the Lightless.
sources: section 'The Winter of the World': Order of the Djinn founded by the Maraketh survivors and the Clayshaper
event entry 'Founding of the Order of the Djinn'

edges.description: Sekhema Deshret joins High Templar Voll's Purity Rebellion in exchange for the return of the Vastiri Plains.
sources: event entry 'Purity Rebellion' (Sekhema Deshret listed among the leaders)

edges.description: The Maraketh under Sekhema Deshret make a pact with Voll for their support in exchange for the Vastiri Plains.
Sekhema Deshret seals the Highgate mines with the Beast inside, as the Maraketh page records.
sources: section 'Deshret': 'sealed the entrance to The Mines'

edges.description: Maraketh akhara contest rule of Highgate; the Sekhema Feather goes to Tasuni or Irasha after Kira's rite is broken up.
Sekhema Asenath, the Golden Sekhema, is one of the Maraketh's Sekhemas (leaders) and was murdered while wearing the Wings of Vastiri.
sources: section 'Hector Titucius': killed Sekhema Asenath and took the Wings of Vastiri

edges.description: Sekhema Lundara, twin of Solerai, is one of the Maraketh's Sekhemas.
Kira is a Maraketh warrior who leads a dekhara and kidnaps Sekhema Oyun for her rite to Garukhan.
sources: section 'Notable members': 'Kira (later an enemy - Kira, Servant of Garukhan)'
event entry 'The Ruler of Highgate': Kira and her dekhara kidnap Oyun; Kira is Tasuni's sister

edges.description: Irasha is the Maraketh akhara of Highgate and a rival of Tasuni for rule after Oyun's disappearance.
sources: event entry 'The Ruler of Highgate': Irasha, akhara of Highgate, rival of Tasuni

edges.description: Sumei is a former Maraketh member listed among the notable members.
The Templar Church sentences Oriathan criminals and ships them to Wraeclast under High Templar Dominus's Blackguards.
sources: event entry 'Sentencing of the Exiles by Oriath'
section 'Lore': Dominus 'responsible for the exile of criminals to Wraeclast'

edges.description: The Templars' High Templar Dominus is killed atop the Sceptre of God in Act 3.
sources: section 'Lore': 'Dominus is later killed atop the Sceptre of God in Act 3'

edges.description: High Templar Avarius, the Templars' vessel of Innocence, is killed in the Templar Courts in Act 5 (Death to Purity quest).
sources: section 'Lore': the Exile 'defeats High Templar Avarius'

edges.description: A Templar named Bannon sacrifices himself to host the reborn Innocence.
sources: section 'Lore': Sin uses 'a Templar named Bannon' as a vessel

edges.description: The Templars shift their base to the unaffected island of Oriath and develop a theocracy there.
sources: section 'Lore': 'The Order of the Templar shifted their base of operations to the unaffected Oriath'

edges.description: High Templar Voll leads the Purity Rebellion of the Templars against Emperor Chitus.
sources: section 'Lore': 'High Templar Voll's Purity Rebellion against Emperor Chitus'

edges.description: High Templar Voll lays siege to Sarn in 1334 IC, the Templar-led assault that ends with Sarn's surrender.
sources: event entry 'Siege of Sarn' (Voll laid siege to Sarn)

edges.description: Baran, one of the Conquerors' antagonists, is a former Templar and brother of Officer Kirac.
sources: node summary: 'Templar elderslayer who hears God's whispers'
section 'Conquerors of the Atlas' (Conquerors): 'One of the new antagonists, Baran, is a former Templar'

edges.description: Bannon is a Templar whom Sin uses as the vessel for Innocence in Act 10.
sources: section 'Lore': 'uses a Templar named Bannon as a vessel'

edges.description: The Ring runs the Rogue Harbour, and the introductory quest sends the Exile into its Heist contracts.
Kurai's first Ring contract, Trial Run, is completed for the Ring in the Rogue Harbour.
The Ring's client contract, Hyrri's Gift, steals the book 'O' Eternal from an Oriathan nobleman's vault.
The Ring's Kurai negotiates with the Vox twins over the stolen book, and the meeting ends in war.
The Ring's Kurai and the Vox twins fail to reach a truce over Hana, and the second meeting ends in hostility.
The Ring's Kurai confronts the Vox twins Vic and Vinny in the final Ring contract, The Twins.
The Three Sisters destroy Kulemak's mortal form and end the Winter of the World.
sources: lead summary: the sisters ended the Winter of the World

edges.description: The sisters' return of the sun ends the Winter of the World; the Maraketh credit Solerai and Lundara, other sources credit Solaris.
Solerai, with Lundara, is the Maraketh name for one of the cross-cultural Three Sisters who ended the Winter of the World.
Lundara, twin of Solerai, is the Maraketh name for one of the Three Sisters; the wiki says Lundara may be Lunaris.
A Gemling Legion Captain gathers the legionnaires at the Grain Gate in Act 8, and the Exile destroys them.
sources: page 'The Gemling Legion': the Captain and legionnaires at the Grain Gate

edges.description: The gemling legionnaires linked to Chitus's master gem die when he is killed.
Gemling legionnaires under Emperor Chitus repel the Purity Rebellion's assault on the Grain Gate.
sources: section 'The Purity Rebellion': the Templars, Ezomytes, Maraketh and Karui march on the Grain Gate; the Gemlings push them back

edges.description: The Cataclysm that Malachai triggers ends the Eternal Empire; Gemlings seem especially affected by its corruption.
Dialla is the Gemling Queen, Malachai's promised concubine whose jewels are set into her spine.
sources: node summary: 'Malachai's concubine and promised Gemling Queen'

edges.description: The Exile kills Shavronne of Umbra, one of the Godless Three, in Axiom Prison.
sources: section 'Shavronne of Umbra': Act 4 and Act 6 forms

edges.description: Maligaro, the Artist (Inquisitor Maligaro's Act 7 form), is killed in the Chamber of Sins so that Sin can harvest his soul.
sources: section 'Inquisitor Maligaro': Maligaro, the Artist in Act 7
quest 'Essence of the Artist' (Act 7): kill Maligaro, the Artist

edges.description: Doedre the Vile, the third of the Godless Three, is killed in Act 8 in the sewers below Sarn so that Sin can harvest her soul.
sources: section 'Doedre Stamatis': Doedre the Vile in Act 8
quest 'Essence of the Hag' (Act 8): kill Doedre the Vile

edges.description: Vaal Architect mini-bosses appear during the Incursion league's visits to the Temple of Atzoatl.
Kitava's cultists take over the Karui slave revolt after Innocence dies and Kitava reawakens.
sources: lead: the cultists 'appear after the vessel of Innocence dies in the middle of Act 5'
event entry 'Kitava Reawakens and Defeats the Exile'

edges.description: Vorici is a Silent Brother of the Brotherhood of Silence.
House Cyaxan's founder Kylian is one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Tyndarus in the Trarthan War of Independence.
sources: node summary of Kylian: 'one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus'

edges.description: The first-generation Trarthan Great Houses lead the rebellion against Phrecius that ends in Trarthus's warlords' executions.
sources: event entry 'Trarthan Rebellion against Phrecius (870 IC)'

edges.description: Kaom, chieftain of the Ngamahu tribe, makes a pact with Voll in exchange for Karui sovereignty over the south shore.
sources: section 'Karui chieftains': Kaom, chieftain of the Ngamahu tribe

edges.description: Kaom leads 500 Ngamahu warriors to Highgate, is deceived by the Beast, and dies there.
sources: event entry 'Kaom's march on Highgate and death'

edges.description: The Ngamahu tribe offers its unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors, led by its chieftain's team.
sources: section 'Karui chieftains' and the Ancestors' tribal trial

edges.description: The Tawhoa tribe competes in the Trial of the Ancestors under its chieftain Maata.
sources: section 'Karui chieftains': Maata, chieftain of the Tawhoa tribe

edges.description: The Order of the Chalice, through High Priest Uhtred, takes part in the First Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast, which was led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved.
sources: event entry 'First Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast' (Uhtred, Order of the Chalice)

edges.description: High Priest Uhtred has a dozen priests stab Olroth, the priesthood conspiracy.
Uhtred is branded a traitor after the loss of the Triskelion Flame and flees.
sources: event entry 'Loss of the Triskelion Flame'

edges.description: Meridian Free Traders agent Raulf explains recruitment during the Kingsmarch tutorial.
Aldur, first Runefather, founded the Runefathers as his chosen apprentices in runesmithing.
sources: node summary: 'first King of Kalguur and first Runefather'

edges.description: Atziri is the last Queen of the Vaal and rules their empire as its sovereign until the Vaal Cataclysm.
sources: section 'Reign of Queen Atziri' / 'Early reign': 'Queen Atziri was the last Queen of the Vaal'

edges.description: Doryani served the Vaal crown as Atziri's premier thaumaturgist and ran the project that led to the Vaal Cataclysm.
sources: section 'Reign of Queen Atziri' / 'Zerphi': 'Atziri tasked her premier thaumaturgist Doryani'

edges.description: Kishara was a Vaal explorer of Atziri's time who fell out of favour before the Vaal fall.
Zerphi was a Vaalish noble whose longevity drew Atziri's attention during her reign.
Jaetai is named only in the flavour text of Atziri's Foible; the item's name suggests she was an advisor to Atziri, placing her within the Vaal court.
Atalui is a Vaal priestess known only from item flavour text.
The Vaal Architects (Incursion mini-boss group) are listed among the Vaal figures; the Royal Architect Xipocado is tied to the Temple of Atzoatl.
The Vaal were destroyed in the Vaal Cataclysm, which left only 3,126 survivors.
sources: section 'Fall of the Vaal' / 'The Vaal Cataclysm'

edges.description: The Vaal made first contact with the Azmeri and introduced agriculture and literacy to them.
Vaal who died in the Cataclysm are said to keep sacrificing themselves to Atziri in her crimson nightmare realm (PoE2 account).
sources: section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' / PoE2 account: 'Atziri\'s "crimson nightmare" realm'

edges.description: The Syndicate's Betrayal-league Act 1 fortifications are dismantled as Jun asks the Exile to break down the door.
sources: section 'Quest logs': 'Jun wants you to help her find and dismantle the Immortal Syndicate fortifications'

edges.description: The Exile intercepts an Immortal Syndicate transport in the Betrayal-league Act 1 quest Cutting Off the Supply.
sources: Header: 'was a quest in Act 1 exclusive to the Betrayal league'; Version history 3.6.0 'Removed from the game'

edges.description: Kastov, Governor of Stridevolf, joined High Templar Voll's Purity Rebellion in 1333 IC.
sources: section 'Purity Rebellion' / Kastov joins Voll in 1333 IC

edges.description: The Purity Rebellion, led by Voll and Victario, is the uprising against Chitus' gem-based thaumatocracy.
The Purity Rebellion launched the rebel assault at the Grain Gate, which Chitus' gemlings repulsed.
High Templar Voll laid siege to Sarn on behalf of the Purity Rebellion in Divini 1334 IC.
Cadiro Perandus negotiated the unconditional surrender of Sarn to the Purity Rebellion's leader Voll.
Voll, leader of the Purity Rebellion, was crowned Emperor in Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC.
Voll and Victario made a pact with King Kaom, promising Karui sovereignty over the south in exchange for support.
Voll pledged the Vastiri Plains to Sekhema Deshret in return for Maraketh support for the Rebellion.
Voll spared Malachai, a decision taken by the Rebellion's leadership in the fall of the Eternal Empire.
Thane Rigwald rallied the Ezomytes of Ezomyr against the Eternal Empire during the 1333 IC rebellion.
The Ezomytes won the 1333 IC Bloody Flowers Rebellion at Glarryn against the Empire.
Ezomyte rebels joined the Purity Rebellion's siege of Sarn in 1334 IC.
sources: section 'Siege of Sarn' (Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh allies)

edges.description: Ezomytes took part in the rebel assault at the Grain Gate led by Victario.
sources: section 'Battle at the Grain Gate' (Templars, Ezomytes, Maraketh and Karui)

edges.description: Ezomytes were allied to the Purity Rebellion during the 1333-1334 IC uprising.
Ailith, First of the Keepers, leads the Keepers of the Flame from the Monastery.
sources: section 'Keepers of the Flame' / Ailith as founder and leader

edges.description: The Keepers burn the Hiveborn barrier at the Mud Flats and bond the Genesis Tree in the Act 6 Breach quest Into the Breach.
sources: page summary: Ailith's flame burns the Hiveborn barrier; Exile bonds the Genesis Tree

edges.description: Ixan Keita was one of the four Great Founders of the Trarthan Great Houses and rebelled against Tyndarus Phrecius.
Kylian Cyaxan was one of the four Great Founders of the Trarthan Great Houses who rebelled against Tyndarus Phrecius.
Ratha Azadi was one of the four Great Founders of the Trarthan Great Houses who rebelled against Tyndarus Phrecius.
Quilon Bardiya was one of the four Great Founders of the Trarthan Great Houses who rebelled against Tyndarus Phrecius.
The Trarthans rose against Tyndarus Phrecius in the 870-872 IC War of Independence.
Four first-generation Trarthans led the 870 IC rebellion against the Phrecian occupation of Trarthus.
Trarthan Great Houses fought the Merchant Wars and War of the Great Families, ending in the Merchant Council.
sources: section 'Merchant Wars and War of the Great Families'

edges.description: Trarthan mercenaries are lawless Trarthan veterans who can be hired as allies in the Mercenaries league.
House Bardiya traces its founding to Quilon Bardiya, one of the Great Founders who led the 870-872 IC revolt.
sources: section 'History' / Quilon Bardiya as Great Founder

edges.description: House Bardiya's founder Quilon Bardiya was among the four Trarthans who led the 870 IC rebellion.
Varashta, the Winter Sekhema, opposes the Afarud, a rogue Faridun sect she says disgusts her.
sources: dialogue: 'the Afarud disgust me'; 'you will have to fight the Afarud'

edges.description: The Karui rebellion under Utula demands Casticus' eyes, which the Exile takes to enter the Templar Courts.
sources: page 'The Key to Freedom' / Utula demands Casticus' eyes

edges.description: Utula leads the Karui slave rebellion in completing the King's Feast ritual that summons Kitava.
sources: page 'The King s Feast' / Utula completes the ritual

edges.description: The Arohongui tribe, led by its chieftain, fields a team in the Trial of the Ancestors and offers its unique item.
sources: section 'Trial of the Ancestors' / tribe rewards

edges.description: The Ramako tribe, led by its chieftain, fields a team in the Trial of the Ancestors and offers its unique item.
sources: section 'Trial of the Ancestors' / tribe rewards

edges.description: The Tukohama tribe, led by its chieftain, fields a team in the Trial of the Ancestors and offers its unique item.
sources: section 'Trial of the Ancestors' / 'Unique items': Akoya's Gaze (tribe item)

edges.description: Rin Yuushu is an Immortal Syndicate member who, according to Jun's dialogue, belonged to the Mutewind warband.
sources: page body: 'Based on Jun's dialogue, Rin was a member of Mutewind'

edges.description: Cardinal Sanctus Vox is the ancestor of the Vox family, an Oriathan noble house.
sources: page intro: ancestor of the Vox family

edges.description: The Vox twins' dealings in Contract: The Rescue end with the Vox family ordered dead after they killed Hana.
sources: 'The Rescue' section and 'Return To Rogue Harbour' ('They killed Hana')

edges.description: The haunted dead of House Nevalius become buryable for grave crafting in the Necropolis league, which introduced the family-based unique 'Nevalius Inheritance'.
sources: section 'Items' / 'Unique items': Nevalius Inheritance (four haunted members of one family)

edges.description: The Remembrancers recorded the First Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast.
sources: section 'Society': Remembrancers documented the Kalguur's explorations in foreign lands

edges.description: The Prime Remembrancer's logbooks documented the Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast, which set up outposts and then collapsed.
sources: section 'Expedition to Wraeclast' / Prime Remembrancer logbook lore

edges.description: The Prime Remembrancer's logbooks record the Kalguuran expedition that The Lost Expedition quest uncovers through the Ancient Kalguuran texts.
sources: section 'Expedition to Wraeclast' / Prime Remembrancer logbook lore (quest page: 'Ancient Kalguuran texts')

edges.description: Malachai, Laureate Thaumaturge, served the imperial court and built the gemling legions for the Empire.
Lazhwar, an archbishop of the Eternal Faith who experimented with thaumaturgy, is listed among the Empire's thaumaturgists as Malachai's precursor.
sources: section 'Members' / Thaumaturgists: 'Lazhwar, thaumaturge precursor to Malachai'

edges.description: Doedre was one of the Godless Three thaumaturgists serving the Eternal Empire under Malachai.
sources: section 'Members' / Thaumaturgists: 'Doedre, of the Godless Three'

edges.description: Maligaro, the Inquisitor flesh artist, was one of the Godless Three in the Empire's thaumaturgist circle.
sources: section 'Members' / Thaumaturgists: 'Maligaro, of the Godless Three'

edges.description: Shavronne was one of the Godless Three thaumaturgists who studied under Malachai.
sources: section 'Members' / Thaumaturgists: 'Shavronne, of the Godless Three'

edges.description: Lord Mayor Ondar, a Sarn official, was an Eternal Empire member who betrayed and killed Emperor Chitus during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons celebration in the Purity Rebellion.
sources: section 'Members' / Purity Rebellion rebels: 'Lord Mayor Ondar, betrayer of Chitus'

edges.description: Victario, the Sarn poet, was an Eternal citizen who backed Voll's Purity Rebellion and led the rebel assault on the Grain Gate against Chitus.
sources: section 'Members' / Purity Rebellion rebels: 'Victario, the People's Poet'; section 'Battle at the Grain Gate' (Victario's forces)

edges.description: Gaius Sentari served the Empire as its Supreme Servant and ran the civilization camps near Highgate.
sources: section 'Members' / Chitus Perandus' court: 'Gaius Sentari, Supreme Servant to the Empire'

edges.description: General Adus, commander of Highgate, was an Eternal officer who later joined Voll's rebellion.
sources: section 'Members' / Purity Rebellion rebels: 'Adus, Commander of Highgate'

edges.description: Tarcus Veruso, Prima Imperialus, ruled the Empire he founded as its first Emperor.
sources: section 'Members' / Emperors: 'Tarcus Veruso, founder of the Eternal Empire'

edges.description: Alano Phrecia was crowned Emperor after defeating the dark being and founded the Phrecian line of emperors.
Izaro was the last Phrecian emperor and ruled the Empire until the Labyrinth succession.
sources: section 'Reign of Izaro' / Emperors: 'Izaro, creator of The Lord's Labyrinth'

edges.description: Romira was an Emperor whose atrocities led to his deposition in the Night of a Thousand Ribbons.
sources: section 'Reign of Romira Phrecian' / Emperors: 'Romira, deposed by the Night of a Thousand Ribbons'

edges.description: Tyndarus Phrecius reigned as Emperor during the Trarthan war of independence.
sources: section 'Members' / Emperors: 'Tyndarus, who reigned during Trarthus' war of independence'

edges.description: The Perandus family was the wealthiest merchant family inside the Eternal Empire.
sources: section 'Members' / 'Perandus family' (listed among the Empire's families)

edges.description: The Empire was founded in 1 IC when Tarcus Veruso led the Azmeri into the lands left by the Vaal.
Sarn was burned in protest against Romira, and the Night was later celebrated as a festival.
sources: section 'Reign of Romira Phrecian' / 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'

edges.description: The Empire's legions drove the dark being into its lair and sealed it away under Alano Phrecia.
A portion of the Empire was cast into perpetual night during the reign of Caspiro.
The Empire's succession was decided by Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth, which Chitus won by rigging.
Chitus was crowned Emperor of the Eternal Empire after winning the Labyrinth.
Emperor Chitus was assassinated by Ondar during the Purity Rebellion.
The Empire was split by the Purity Rebellion led by High Templar Voll, with Victario's support, against Emperor Chitus.
sources: section 'Reign of Chitus' / Purity Rebellion rebels

edges.description: The Empire's gemling legions under Chitus repulsed the rebel assault at the Grain Gate.
sources: section 'Purity Rebellion' / Battle at the Grain Gate

edges.description: Sarn, the Empire's capital, was besieged by Voll's rebel forces in 1334 IC.
Voll of Thebrus was crowned Emperor after the Purity Rebellion overthrew Chitus.
Phrecian legions of the Empire occupied Trarthus in 870 IC and executed its warlords.
Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius fought the Trarthan war of independence, which the Empire lost.
Yeena is listed among the notable Azmeri humans.
Silk is listed among the notable Azmeri humans.
Eighty thousand Azmeri under Tarcus Veruso descended into the former Vaal lands and founded the Empire.
sources: section 'Founding the Eternal Empire' / 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)'

edges.description: The Azmeri turned their backs on Oshabi when the land's whispers fell silent, leaving her alone.
sources: Oshabi page, 'Lifeforce'/'The Grove' quotes: 'my brothers and sisters turned their backs on me'

edges.description: The Lightless broke through to the surface through the Vastiri Plains during the Winter of the World.
The Lightless invaded the surface and attacked the Maraketh.
Kulemak's army of possessed golems toppled the primeval civilisation.
Kulemak struck a deal with Ahn for a stone golem, which he bound with souls to become the vessel of his possessed army; Aul later sealed the golems in crystal.
sources: section 'Kulemak' (deal with Ahn for a stone golem; Aul's crystal seal)

edges.description: The Winter of the World ended when the Lightless war was ended by the Three Sisters.
sources: section 'Winter of the World' (ended by the Three Sisters)

edges.description: Zana recruited a team of exiles, later known as the Elderslayers, to track down the Elder across the Atlas.
sources: section 'The Elderslayers' / 'Defeat of the Elder' (Zana assembled the group; 'later known as the Elderslayers')

edges.description: After the group split up, the former Elderslayers went mad within the Atlas, which is the Conquerors of the Atlas storyline.
sources: section 'Conquerors of the Atlas' (former Elderslayers split and went mad within the Atlas)

edges.description: Sirus, the group's leader, returned with a great storm and entered Oriath through his own map device.
sources: section 'Sirus' ('Sirus returned with a great storm'; Sirus 'the leader of the group')

edges.description: Sirus, the former Elderslayers' leader, entered Oriath and the city was burned to the ground in the fight that followed.
sources: section 'Sirus' ('Oriath was burned to the ground')

edges.description: Julius Perandus was the father of Emperor Chitus within the Perandus family.
Cadiro used Perandus wealth to rig Izaro's Labyrinth in Chitus' favour.
Chitus Perandus ascended to the throne through the Perandus family's manoeuvring.
Chitus Perandus was assassinated during the Purity Rebellion.
The Necropolis-dead House Perandus are Perandus family debtors who were bound in servitude to Cadiro after death.
sources: Drusia, Kostian, Lucilius, Quintio (Necropolis league corpses); debtors 'trapped ... in eternal servitude to Cadiro after their deaths'

edges.description: The Phrecian line of emperors, from Alano Phrecia to Izaro, ruled the Eternal Empire; the Necropolis House Phrecia takes its name from it.
sources: section 'Reign of Alano Phrecia' ('unbroken line of Phrecia emperors')

edges.description: Ixan Keita declared Korathin the Trarthan capital in 872 IC, and its construction began with slave labour.
sources: section 'History' / Korathin declared by Ixan Keita (872 IC)

edges.description: Ixan Keita, founder of House Keita, was one of the Great Founders who led the Trarthan war of independence against the Empire.
sources: section 'History' (war led by the four Great Founders; Tyndarus capitulated after two years)

edges.description: Medved, leader of the Druids of the Broken Circle, went alone to challenge the horror leader and did not return.
sources: Kalguur expedition section: 'Medved travelled into the night to challenge the new leader, and did not return'

edges.description: The Hinekora tribe fields a team in the Trial of the Ancestors.

edges.description: The Black Scythes were the Kalguuran mercenary arbalists attached to the expedition.
sources: section 'Society' ('The Black Scythe were mercenaries led by Vorana ... in the expedition group')

edges.description: The Black Scythes defended the Kalguuran expedition group on its voyage to Wraeclast.
sources: section 'Society' ('responsible for defense and offense in the expedition group')

edges.description: Vorana, leader of the Black Scythes, tried to draw back the starlight barrier; instead it vanished and the Triskelion Flame was found gone from its altar.
sources: Kalguur expedition section: Vorana's plan to draw back the starlight barrier; 'the starlight barrier entirely vanished ... altar empty'

edges.description: Vorana, leader of the Black Scythes, gave Medved two gem-socketed axes before his challenge.
sources: Kalguur expedition section: Vorana 'offered a gift of two axes with gems affixed'

edges.description: Ebony Legion and Blackguards are the Templar soldiers of Dominus.
sources: section 'Current Templars and subordinates' ('The Blackguards and the Ebony Legion'; Blackguards are Templar soldiers under Dominus)
